Additionally, generalized linear interpolation to 3D space to reconstruct signals, enabling coherent combining across wideband and suppressing beam squint for improved delay estimation accuracy.

problem_description: Traditional matrix-based channel estimation techniques lose relational information between different dimensions time, frequency, space of received signals and are highly susceptible to noise, especially at low SNR.
skill_point_name: Tensor-based Channel Parameter Estimation
skill_point_description: Proposed a new tensor-based channel estimation algorithm that arranges received signals in a tensor form. This allows for suppressing receiver noises in all dimensions time, frequency, and space, leading to substantially higher estimation accuracy compared to existing matrix-based techniques, even at low SNR, by preserving the multi-dimensional structure of signals.

problem_description: Achieving massive access capability in mIoT networks with low cost and power consumption using large antenna arrays is challenging, as fully digital solutions are impractical due to excessive RF chain requirements.
skill_point_name: Nested Hybrid Cylindrical Array Design for mIoT
skill_point_description: Developed a novel nested hybrid UCyA design that leverages sparse array techniques. This design enables accurate angle estimation for a large number of devices with significantly fewer RF chains than antennas, addressing the massive access requirements of mIoT networks while drastically reducing hardware cost and power consumption through a sparse RF-chain connection network.

problem_description: Coherent signals in sparse array systems can lead to rank deficiency in the signal subspace, hindering accurate DOA estimation by subspace-based algorithms. Additionally, existing methods may compromise the array's symmetric structure, reducing accuracy.
skill_point_name: Tensor n-Rank Enhancement and 2D-DOA Estimation for Sparse Arrays
skill_point_description: Introduced a spatial smoothing-based method to enhance the n-rank of the signal tensor model for nested hybrid UCyAs, ensuring proper decomposition of signal and noise subspaces even with coherent signals. Combined this with a tensor-based 2D-DOA estimation algorithm, Tensor TLS-ESPRIT and Tensor MUSIC, that operates directly on the signal data model, preserving the symmetric structure and significantly improving estimation accuracy.

problem_description: Building a scalable and cost-effective infrastructure for capturing, processing, and analyzing WiFi measurements across a city, while also addressing privacy concerns and ensuring data accessibility.
skill_point_name: Scalable WiFi Sensing and Cloud Infrastructure MobIntel
skill_point_description: Developed and deployed MobIntel, a scalable WiFi sensing infrastructure comprising low-cost WiFi probe request sensors and a cloud platform for data ingestion, processing, aggregation, presentation, and archival. This includes a web portal for mobility insights, for example, weekly activity patterns and repeat visitor detection, and data export tools, demonstrated by deploying 54 sensors in a real-world urban environment, Clematis Street, West Palm Beach.

problem_description: Achieving accurate device localization with limited data samples and in environments with multipath effects, surpassing the limitations of RSSI-based methods.
skill_point_name: Few-Sample CSI-Based Localization MobLoc
skill_point_description: Introduced MobLoc, a CSI-based localization method utilizing MUSIC pseudospectrum estimates for fingerprinting. Designed to operate effectively with few samples and capable of sparse environment surveying, MobLoc achieves meter-level localization accuracy by leveraging the entire pseudospectrum to mitigate multipath effects, for example, 0.33m median error in simple environments.

problem_description: Realizing fast and robust Direction of Arrival DoA estimation using a single measurement snapshot, particularly in massive MIMO systems, while overcoming spatial aliasing and calibration challenges.
skill_point_name: Single-Sample Hankel SVD for DoA Estimation
skill_point_description: Evaluated a novel Hankel Singular Value Decomposition SVD method for single-sample DoA estimation. This method demonstrates superior performance over the traditional MUSIC algorithm in both azimuth and elevation estimation, effectively mitigating spatial aliasing and robustly handling imperfect data calibration, enabling faster and more granular real-time WiFi analysis.

problem_description: Mitigating MAC address randomization to enable persistent device re-identification and longitudinal analysis of mobility patterns.
skill_point_name: Deep Learning-Based WiFi Device Fingerprinting and Re-identification MobRFFI
skill_point_description: Developed MobRFFI, a novel framework for WiFi device fingerprinting and re-identification using deep learning encoder-based model to extract unique features from WiFi chipset hardware impairments derived from preamble spectrograms. This framework achieves high device classification accuracy 94-100% and demonstrates significant improvements in known/unknown device classification by combining fingerprints from multiple receivers, effectively overcoming MAC address randomization.

problem_description: Providing a granular, multi-receiver dataset for advanced WiFi device fingerprinting research, which is crucial for evaluating and developing robust re-identification methods.
skill_point_name: Collection and Publication of Multi-Receiver WiFi Fingerprinting Dataset MobRFFI Dataset
skill_point_description: Collected and published a novel 5.7 TB MobRFFI dataset specifically designed for granular multi-receiver WiFi device fingerprinting evaluation. This dataset facilitated experiments demonstrating how combining fingerprints from multiple receivers significantly boots re-identification performance in both single-day and multi-day scenarios, addressing a critical gap in existing datasets.

problem_description: Traditional Wi-Fi localization algorithms struggle in complex indoor environments with multipath and NLoS, leading to significant errors, especially in corner cases, and accurate indoor maps are scarce.
skill_point_name: DLoc: Machine Learning-based Wi-Fi Localization
skill_point_description: Developed DLoc, a novel deep learning framework that frames localization as an image translation problem, creating a unique image representation for RF-data derived from Channel State Information CSI. DLoc achieves decimeter-level accuracy, even in challenging multipath-rich or Non-Line-of-Sight NLoS environments, and corrects for time-of-flight offsets without extra client instrumentation. It leverages convolutional neural networks and integrates domain knowledge from Wi-Fi positioning, tested with an autonomous robot MapFind and validated across diverse real-world scenarios, leading to a patent.

problem_description: Indoor navigation and accurate multi-point wireless localization systems critically rely on precise knowledge of Wi-Fi Access Point AP locations, antenna placements, and deployment orientations, which are difficult and labor-intensive to obtain manually.
skill_point_name: LocAP: Autonomous Access Point Attribute Localization
skill_point_description: Designed LocAP, an autonomous system capable of determining Wi-Fi AP location attributes location, antenna separation, and orientation with high precision. It achieves centimeter-level AP localization and millimeter-level antenna geometry prediction by leveraging CSI data collected by the MapFind robot across numerous locations. LocAP employs a weighted least squares approach that incorporates a confidence metric for robot pose estimates, effectively overcoming inaccuracies inherent in SLAM systems. This enables automated, accurate mapping of existing Wi-Fi infrastructure for improved user localization without manual effort.

problem_description: Bluetooth Low Energy BLE localization systems traditionally rely on Received Signal Strength Indication RSSI, which is inaccurate, unstable in multipath conditions, and susceptible to dynamic environment changes, limiting their utility for precise indoor tracking.
skill_point_name: BLoc: CSI-based BLE Sub-meter Localization
skill_point_description: Developed BLoc, the first system to enable sub-meter localization accuracy for BLE devices by using Channel State Information CSI, encompassing both signal strength and phase. BLoc innovates by designing special BLE packets with long sequences of bits for stable frequency measurement, stitching together CSI across multiple hopping frequency bands spanning 80 MHz to emulate a wideband signal, and developing a novel collaborative algorithm to eliminate random phase offsets across channels. It also includes an advanced multipath elimination algorithm that identifies direct paths based on shortest distance and spatial entropy, validated to significantly outperform RSSI-based methods in multipath-rich environments.

problem_description: Wi-Fi sensing systems, particularly those using Angle-of-Arrival AoA measurements, can infer users' precise indoor locations without their consent, posing significant privacy risks and enabling unwanted tracking, while existing defenses often degrade communication quality.
skill_point_name: MIRAGE: RF-Privacy Preservation
skill_point_description: Developed 'MIRAGE,' an algorithm that allows Wi-Fi users to protect their location privacy against passive AoA-based snooping attacks without compromising Wi-Fi communication quality SNR or throughput. MIRAGE's core innovation is to subtly manipulate the transmitted Wi-Fi signal to make the direct path appear to travel a longer distance than reflected paths. This 'mirage' confuses the attacker's localization algorithms by creating a highly incorrect location estimate up to 10m error in testing, while being compliant with Wi-Fi protocols and not requiring explicit collaboration from the access point. It achieves this by selectively delaying the direct path signal through precoding, ensuring the correct AoA cannot be reliably extracted.

problem_description: Collecting large-scale, labeled Wi-Fi Channel State Information CSI data with accurate ground truth for training machine learning models in diverse indoor environments is time-consuming, expensive, and requires significant manual effort.
skill_point_name: MapFind: Autonomous Indoor Mapping and Data Collection Platform
skill_point_description: Designed and implemented MapFind, an autonomous robot platform for efficient and accurate collection of geolocated Wi-Fi CSI data and physical indoor maps. Equipped with LIDAR, RGB-D cameras, and odometry, MapFind uses state-of-the-art SLAM algorithms like RTAB-Map and Cartographer to automatically map complex indoor environments with fine detail. A key innovation is its path planning algorithm, which optimizes coverage to maximize data diversity while minimizing traversal time, for example, mapping 1500 sq. ft. in 20 minutes versus 17 hours manually, providing high-quality, large-scale labeled datasets crucial for training robust ML-based localization systems like DLoc and LocAP.

problem_description: Traditional signal parameter estimation techniques for wireless communication systems, especially for parameters like channel profile, Doppler shift, and SNR, face challenges in meeting the stringent accuracy and latency requirements of modern 5G and LTE systems due to model complexity and reliance on known pilot signals, which often leads to reduced spectral efficiency.
skill_point_name: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Spatial and Temporal Feature Learning
skill_point_description: Developed and utilized a novel hybrid Convolutional Neural Network CNN and Long Short-Term Memory LSTM model to learn both spatial features within each input data sample and temporal features across sequences of input samples. This architectural innovation significantly enhanced prediction accuracy for wireless signal parameters channel profile, Doppler shift, and SNR in complex LTE and 5G environments, outperforming traditional methods and isolated CNN/LSTM approaches.

problem_description: Deep Learning models often suffer from insufficient or diverse input data, limiting their ability to generalize and make robust predictions, especially when dealing with complex real-world wireless environments characterized by diverse impairments.
skill_point_name: Input Diversity for Enhanced Prediction Accuracy
skill_point_description: Implemented and validated an 'input diversity' technique, involving the use of multiple inputs per prediction, for example, sequences of data. This approach, leveraging both spatial and temporal diversity, enabled the model to extract more differentiation features and significantly improved prediction accuracy across all investigated wireless signal parameters. Various fusion methods were explored, with the Sequence method being identified as particularly effective due to its ability to handle inter-input correlations.

problem_description: Complex multi-class prediction tasks in Deep Learning can lead to high uncertainty and lower accuracy, especially when dealing with a wide range of possible discrete values for wireless signal parameters.
skill_point_name: Binary Prediction for Uncertainty Reduction and Accuracy Enhancement
skill_point_description: Introduced and successfully applied a 'binary prediction' technique to reduce prediction uncertainty and enhance accuracy. Instead of a single multi-class classifier predicting one label from a wide range, multiple binary classifiers were used, each predicting whether a parameter is less than or greater than/equal to a specific target value. This 'divide and conquer' approach proved effective in cases where traditional multi-class prediction yielded unacceptable performance, significantly boosting accuracy, for example, for 5G channel profile and Doppler shift predictions.

problem_description: Traditional wireless signal parameter estimation techniques often require known pilot signals, a data-aided approach, which consume spectral resources and increase latency, hindering spectral efficiency in modern communication systems.
skill_point_name: Non-Data-Aided NDA Prediction for Spectral Efficiency
skill_point_description: Developed a methodology that enables the prediction of wireless signal parameters using random payload inputs non-data-aided NDA, eliminating the need for known pilot signals. This innovation directly enhances spectral efficiency by freeing up resources typically allocated for pilot transmissions, while maintaining high prediction accuracy e.g., 95% validation.

problem_description: Ensuring the practicality and robustness of deep learning models for wireless applications requires validation against comprehensive and realistic simulated environments that account for various impairments and system complexities.
skill_point_name: Robust Validation with Comprehensive Real-World Wireless Environment Parameterizations
skill_point_description: The proposed methodology was robustly validated through extensive simulations of 5G and LTE communication systems. The simulations incorporated comprehensive real-world environment parameterizations, including randomly selected modulation types QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM, variable Doppler shifts 0-550 Hz, SNR variations -10 to 20 dB, and diverse channel profiles LTE: EPA, EVA, ETU; 5G: TDL-A to TDL-E. This rigorous validation process confirmed the method's high prediction accuracy around 95% and its applicability in dynamic and impaired wireless conditions.

problem_description: Underwater acoustic UWA communication channels exhibit significant spatial and temporal variations due to environmental conditions, posing challenges for UWA networking and applications. Existing channel modeling methods often work offline and struggle with real-time adaptation.
skill_point_name: Online Data-Driven Channel Modeling and Prediction
skill_point_description: Developed a data-driven approach for online modeling and prediction of slowly-varying channel parameters by exploiting their inherent temporal correlation and correlation with environmental conditions. The temporal evolution of channel statistics is modeled as a summation of a time-invariant component, an environmental process, and a Markov latent process. A low-complexity recursive algorithm, based on the EM algorithm, is developed to estimate unknown model parameters and predict channel parameters in real-time. This approach is further extended to seasonal channels by introducing a multiplicative seasonal AR process.

problem_description: Inhomogeneity of sound speed distribution in underwater environments due to stratification/refraction significantly impacts AUV communications and acoustic signaling-based AUV localization, as it leads to non-straight line wave propagation.
skill_point_name: Joint AUV Tracking and Sound Speed Estimation using Factor Graphs
skill_point_description: Developed a distributed and cooperative algorithm for joint sound speed estimation and AUV tracking based on time-of-flight TOF measurements among AUVs. The joint probability distribution of TOF measurements, sound speed parameters, and AUV locations is represented by a factor graph. A Gaussian message passing GMP algorithm is proposed after linearizing nonlinear measurement models, enabling accurate tracking of AUV locations and sound speed parameters, even with sound speed stratification.

problem_description: Accurate characterization of underwater acoustic channels in diverse freshwater environments—stationary, mobile, under-ice—is crucial for designing effective acoustic transceivers, yet such detailed experimental investigations are limited compared to oceanic channels.
skill_point_name: Extensive Experimental UWA Channel Characterization
skill_point_description: Conducted extensive field experiments in the Great Lakes region to characterize three types of freshwater river/lake acoustic channels: stationary, mobile, and under-ice. Analyzed statistical channel variations and sound propagation loss, comparing them with oceanic channels. Identified key differences such as larger temporal coherence, higher correlation among densely distributed channel paths, and less sound absorption loss in freshwater, and more deterministic behavior and less severe variations multipath, Doppler in under-ice channels.

problem_description: The presence of periodic dynamics or seasonality in underwater acoustic channels, for example, diurnal patterns, is not adequately captured by traditional models, leading to suboptimal prediction performance.
skill_point_name: Modeling and Prediction for Seasonal UWA Channels
skill_point_description: Extended the core online modeling and prediction framework to explicitly account for seasonal variations in UWA channels. This involves introducing a multiplicative seasonal autoregressive AR process to the latent process modeling. A low-cost recursive algorithm is developed to handle the increased complexity, allowing for superior modeling and prediction performance by exploiting the seasonal correlation not addressed in non-seasonal models.

problem_description: Traditional sound speed inversion methods, for example ocean tomography, are computationally intensive, often require extensive field measurements, for example hydrophone arrays, and are typically suitable only for offline processing, lacking real-time applicability for mobile networks.
skill_point_name: Distributed and Memory-Efficient Sound Speed Field Estimation in Mobile Networks
skill_point_description: Proposed an approach that specifically considers the inhomogeneity of the sound speed field, including spatio-temporal variations modeled as a Gaussian random field, and integrates its estimation with AUV tracking in a distributed manner. It addresses computational and memory constraints by temporally and spatially truncating correlated observations in the Gaussian process, making it suitable for online implementation in resource-limited mobile sensor networks. The method relies on acoustic measurements (Time of Flight) collected by maneuvering AUVs rather than specialized array measurements.

problem_description: Traditional RFID systems in multipath environments suffer from distorted signal fingerprints and lack accurate region-of-interest object recognition for moving objects, due to multipath interference, frequency-dependent hardware characteristics, and RF phase periodicity.
skill_point_name: CV-assisted ROI Moving Object Recognition RF-Focus
skill_point_description: Developed RF-Focus, a system that integrates RFID and Computer Vision to recognize and track moving RFID-tagged objects within a region of interest in multipath-prevalent environments. This involved proposing novel RSSI/RF phase-distance models with multipath terms, designing a dual-antenna solution to combat multipath interference, developing a method to estimate and remove frequency-dependent phase shifts caused by hardware characteristics, and creating an innovative fusion algorithm to match 2D camera position proposals with cleaned RF phase for high-accuracy object recognition and localization.

problem_description: Stationary RFID tag localization in 3D space is challenging due to RF phase periodicity causing multiple possible tag positions, and the difficulty in acquiring accurate reader antenna trajectories for mobile systems without predefined paths or pre-deployed tracks.
skill_point_name: CV-assisted Stationary Object 3D Localization RF-MVO
skill_point_description: Introduced RF-MVO, a system that fuses RFID and Computer Vision to locate stationary RFID tags in 3D space without requiring predefined reader antenna trajectories. This skill point involves estimating camera/antenna trajectory using monocular visual odometry techniques, leveraging depth-enabled RF phase to transform camera-view trajectories to real-world coordinates by estimating a scale factor, and proposing a novel DOA-based 3D localization algorithm that avoids exhaustive spatial search. It also includes a coarse-to-fine optimization algorithm for improved accuracy and real-time performance, and utilizes Horizontal Dilution of Precision to select optimal localization results based on tag-antenna geometry.

problem_description: Estimating 3D orientation of RFID-tagged objects using multiple tags is hindered by mutual coupling interference between closely spaced tags and persistent multipath interference in the environment, distorting reported RFID signal fingerprints.
skill_point_name: CV-assisted Two-RFID-Tag Labeled Object 3D Orientation RF-Orien3D
skill_point_description: Designed RF-Orien3D, a system that leverages the 'bad' mutual coupling effect between two closely-spaced RFID tags to estimate the 3D orientation azimuth and elevation of a labeled object in multipath-rich environments. This involved extending RSSI/RF phase-distance models to include mutual coupling and multipath terms, simulating tag radiation patterns from 2D images for analysis, estimating scaled impedance-dependent modulation factors, and developing a CNN-based approach with transfer learning to handle complex multipath effects without extensive real-world data collection.

problem_description: Existing RFID localization solutions often rely on RSSI measurements or require extensive pre-deployment of reference tags or complex robotic platforms with known trajectories, limiting their accuracy and practicality in dynamic environments or large surveillance areas.
skill_point_name: Novel RFID Localization Algorithms with Reduced Computational Complexity
skill_point_description: Developed innovative RFID localization algorithms that overcome limitations of traditional methods. For moving objects RF-Focus, it combines cleaned RF phase with image candidate regions, avoiding exhaustive search of possible trajectories. For stationary objects RF-MVO, it introduces a DOA-based 3D localization method that calculates the intersection of spatial lines, eliminating the need to divide the surveillance region into fine grids and search each cuboid, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead and improving real-time performance for large areas.

problem_description: Accurate estimation of hardware-related phase shifts in RFID systems is challenging due to factors like frequency hopping and the difficulty of precisely measuring tag-to-antenna distances manually, which impacts the reliability of RF phase for localization.
skill_point_name: Multipath Interference-Powered Phase Shift Estimation
skill_point_description: Proposed a novel multipath interference-powered method to accurately estimate hardware-related phase shifts at different operating frequencies. This technique leverages the extended multipath models to measure the tag-to-antenna distance using only one reader antenna and several RFID tags, offering higher accuracy than manual measurements. This calibration is crucial for cleaning raw RF phase data, making it a more reliable indicator for precise object localization and recognition in complex environments.

problem_description: Enhancing real-time routing effectiveness and multi-robot mobility in MANETs under uncertain and complex environments, including attacker presence.
skill_point_name: Distributed Reinforcement Learning for MANET Routing SaRE-MANET
skill_point_description: Developed SaRE-MANET protocol using online reinforcement learning to optimize multi-robot mobility and routing. Introduced mission-oriented metrics to describe network quality and robot mobility interrelation, and formulated the problem as a Markov Decision Process for distributed Q-learning, enabling real-time adaptation in harsh environments.

problem_description: Improving MANET robustness against potential physical and cyber attacks while maintaining routing efficiency and robot mobility.
skill_point_name: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning for Secure MANETs GT-SaRE-MANET
skill_point_description: Designed GT-SaRE-MANET by integrating game theory with online reinforcement learning. This approach models interactions between defenders and attackers, using game-theoretic mission-oriented metrics to optimize routing and robot path planning for enhanced resilience and message delivery in vulnerable tactical environments.

problem_description: Maximizing communication quality in multi-user mmWave MIMO systems under uncertain environments, for example, dynamic users and unknown interference, by utilizing robot mobility as dynamic relays.
skill_point_name: Intelligent Multi-Robot Enhanced mmWave MIMO
skill_point_description: Developed MREI-MU-MIMO system. This involves a novel dynamic codebook for improved channel quantization and reduced beam training complexity, and an online reinforcement learning method to optimize multi-robot-relay distribution for multi-hop coverage and increased data rates in uncertain environments.

problem_description: Handling unknown interference and severe uncertainty, such as radio jamming and dynamic user distribution, in mmWave MIMO systems.
skill_point_name: Game-Theoretic Intelligent mmWave MIMO GT-MU-MIMO
skill_point_description: Created GT-MU-MIMO by combining game theory and machine learning for mobile relay planning in mmWave MIMO. This system uses a dynamic codebook and a game-theoretic online reinforcement learning algorithm to maximize signal coverage and data rate while robustly addressing unknown interference and dynamic conditions.

problem_description: Optimizing complex behaviors, such as path planning and resource allocation, in dynamic, uncertain environments where traditional rule-based or static approaches are insufficient.
skill_point_name: Distributed Deep Q-Network DQN Learning for Autonomous Systems
skill_point_description: Applied and extended Distributed Deep Q-Network learning, a form of reinforcement learning with neural networks, for autonomous multi-robot path planning and optimal relay deployment. This enables robots to learn complex behaviors from environmental feedback, adapt to dynamic changes, and optimize mission-critical objectives, for example, communication quality and attack avoidance, with minimal pre-programmed rules.

problem_description: Maximizing the minimum user data rate and reducing transmission/processing latency in uplink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output NOMA systems with multi-layer superposition transmission.
skill_point_name: Multi-Layer Rate Splitting and SIC Detection Optimization in MU-MIMO NOMA
skill_point_description: Proposes a multi-layer superposition transmission scheme combined with rate splitting and successive interference cancellation detection (MMSE-SIC and MRC-SIC) to approach symmetric capacity, increase minimum user data rates, and effectively reduce maximum transmission and processing latency for UL users. Introduces a two-layer rate splitting algorithm and group SIC detection to further reduce computational complexity.

problem_description: Supporting ultra-reliable and low latency communications for short-packet applications with simultaneous uplink and downlink transmission in NOMA systems.
skill_point_name: Full-Duplex Sparse Code Multiple Access FD-SCMA Design for URLLC
skill_point_description: Develops a novel FD-SCMA scheme that combines full-duplex and sparse code multiple access to allow simultaneous UL and DL transmission. Analyzes its reliability and latency performance in time-invariant flat-fading and frequency-selective fading channels, considering imperfect self-interference suppression and utilizing finite blocklength information theory to calculate error probability.

problem_description: Ensuring reliability of ultra-low latency transmission for massive users in MU-MIMO NOMA systems under severe channel fading, such as shadow fading, and imperfect channel state information CSI.
skill_point_name: Robust MU-MIMO NOMA with Optimized Pilot Allocation under Imperfect CSI
skill_point_description: Investigates MU-MIMO NOMA under perfect and imperfect CSI, focusing on ZF detection. Derives the probability density function pdf of post-processing SNRs under log-normal shadow fading and applies FBL information theory to derive error probability. Proposes a Golden Section Search Method GSSM to optimally determine the length of pilots LoP to minimize error probability and effectively reduce pilot overhead.

problem_description: Analyzing and maintaining reliability while meeting stringent latency constraints for short packet transmissions in 5G-enabled Internet of Things IoT applications.
skill_point_name: Finite Blocklength Information Theory Application for URLLC Performance Analysis
skill_point_description: Systematically applies the recently proposed finite blocklength information theory to analyze the achievable data rate and error probability for short packet transmissions. This approach accurately models the reliability and latency trade-offs, which are critical for IoT applications where traditional Shannon's infinite blocklength theory is insufficient.

problem_description: Reducing access and processing latency in NOMA systems for massive IoT connectivity.
skill_point_name: Grant-Free NOMA and Low-Complexity Multi-User Detection MUD
skill_point_description: Explores grant-free NOMA to eliminate scheduling processes and significantly reduce access latency. Focuses on designing and analyzing low-complexity multi-user detection techniques that can handle complex multi-user interference while minimizing processing latency, which is essential for scaling to massive IoT deployments. Examples of multi-user detection techniques include MMSE-SIC, MRC-SIC, and ZF detection.

problem_description: UAVs in IoT data collection have limited energy and dynamic environments make joint optimization of speed control and energy replenishment challenging, leading to inefficient data collection and energy usage.
skill_point_name: Deep Reinforcement Transfer Learning for UAV Operations D3QL-TL
skill_point_description: Developed a novel Deep Dueling Double Q-learning with Transfer Learning D3QL-TL algorithm. This approach enables dynamic optimization of UAV flying speed and battery replacement activities. It addresses high-dimensional state and action spaces, instability in learning, and slow convergence by incorporating advanced RL techniques D3QL and transfer learning, allowing knowledge sharing between UAVs to reduce learning time and improve learning quality in uncertain environments.

problem_description: Integrated Communications and Sensing ICAS systems in autonomous vehicles face challenges in dynamic environments due to strong influences between sensing and data communication functions, requiring adaptive waveform optimization for concurrent high performance in both.
skill_point_name: AI-enabled Adaptive Waveform Configuration for ICAS i-ICS
skill_point_description: Designed a Markov Decision Process-based framework that allows ICAS-AVs to automatically and adaptively choose optimal waveform structures. This framework addresses the dynamic and uncertain environment by utilizing a Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm, i-ICS, which helps the ICAS-AV learn an optimal policy without prior knowledge of channel quality or data arrival rates, thereby balancing communication efficiency and sensing accuracy.

problem_description: The Metaverse demands enormous, diverse, and correlated resources, posing significant management challenges for its deployment, especially concerning real-time response, dynamic resource demand, and maximizing resource utilization across multiple virtual worlds.
skill_point_name: MetaSlicing: Intelligent Resource Allocation for Metaverse iMSAC
skill_point_description: Introduced MetaSlicing, a novel resource allocation framework that includes application decomposition and MetaInstance techniques. It smartly allocates diverse resource types in a multi-tier computing architecture by grouping applications with common functions to enhance resource utilization. It utilizes a semi-Markov Decision Process sMDP and an intelligent Deep Reinforcement Learning DRL algorithm iMSAC for optimal admission control under high demand dynamics and uncertainties.

problem_description: Traditional anti-eavesdropping methods are resource-intensive, for example, encryption and perfect CSI, making them impractical for resource-constrained devices, and sophisticated eavesdroppers can still bypass them, necessitating a lightweight and effective solution.
skill_point_name: Meta-learning-based Cooperative Ambient Backscatter Communications for Anti-Eavesdropping
skill_point_description: Developed a lightweight anti-eavesdropping framework leveraging Ambient Backscatter communications. It splits a message into two parts, one active and one AmB, making it difficult for eavesdroppers to reconstruct the original message without specific system knowledge. A Deep Learning-based signal detector is developed to decode weak AmB signals without perfect CSI, and a meta-learning technique is applied to enable rapid adaptation to new wireless environments with limited data.

problem_description: Conventional deep learning models often require large amounts of high-quality data for training and struggle with dynamic, uncertain wireless environments, such as changing channel conditions, leading to inefficiencies and the need for frequent retraining.
skill_point_name: Data-Efficient Machine Learning for Dynamic Wireless Environments Meta-learning adaption
skill_point_description: Employed and adapted meta-learning techniques to address the high data requirements and retraining challenges of conventional DL/RL in dynamic wireless environments. This allows models to quickly adapt to new tasks or environments with limited training data by leveraging knowledge gained from similar past tasks, significantly reducing computational complexity, improving learning quality, and enhancing model robustness and applicability in real-world 6G scenarios.

problem_description: Traditional wireless communication relies on perfect channel state information CSI at transmitters CSIT, which is unfeasible in next-generation networks due to prohibitive overhead and delay.
skill_point_name: Broadcast Approach for Distributed Interference Management Partial/No CSIT
skill_point_description: Proposes novel non-orthogonal multiaccess schemes for fading multi-user channels with partial or no CSIT. It leverages a broadcast approach where each transmitter splits its data stream into independently generated coded layers adapted to a specific channel state. The receiver decodes as many layers as the actual channel quality permits, effectively transforming a single-user channel into an equivalent broadcast channel. This approach is applied to single-user energy harvesting channels, multiple access channels MAC, and interference channels IC to characterize performance limits and overcome CSI uncertainty.

problem_description: Optimizing power allocation in energy harvesting systems is complex due to sequential and incremental energy availability, especially when channel state information is unknown or partially known at the transmitter.
skill_point_name: Optimal Resource Allocation for Sequential Resource Access
skill_point_description: Develops an analytical framework for optimal resource allocation over a finite time horizon, where resources like harvested energy are available sequentially and incrementally. The algorithm identifies 'dominant constraints' or time instances where all available resources are fully consumed, breaking the problem into smaller, independently solvable sub-problems. This significantly reduces computational complexity compared to generic convex optimization methods and provides closed-form solutions for various utility functions in energy harvesting systems, including online and offline power allocation policies.

problem_description: In multiple access channels with local CSIT, existing NOMA schemes do not optimally adapt layering to the combined network state, limiting achievable rate regions and efficiency.
skill_point_name: State-Dependent Layering and Decoding for Multi-User MAC with Local CSIT
skill_point_description: Proposes a broadcast strategy for multi-user multiple access channels where each transmitter adapts its codebooks and the number of information layers based on the *combined* network state, not just its own channel state. This dynamic adaptation allows for opportunistic higher rates, increased flexibility in decoding order, and reduced encoding/decoding complexity. It's shown to outperform existing schemes, achieve sum-rate capacity asymptotically, and offers advantages such as fewer encoded layers and adaptive decoding compared to fixed layering approaches.

problem_description: Interference management in Gaussian interference channels traditionally relies on perfect CSIT, but obtaining this information is costly and difficult to scale, especially in a non-asymptotic SNR regime.
skill_point_name: Multi-Layer Superposition Coding for Gaussian Interference Channels No CSIT
skill_point_description: Introduces a distributed interference management approach for Gaussian interference channels where transmitters are completely oblivious to channel states. It utilizes multi-layer superposition coding where each transmitter’s streams are adapted to the *combined interference state* of the entire network. Coupled with an opportunistic successive decoding scheme at receivers, this approach achieves average sum-rates within a constant gap of the sum-rate capacity with full CSIT in the high SNR regime, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating the impact of absent CSIT.

problem_description: Achieving low latency and high reliability in wireless networks, for example IoT, is critical, but conventional NOMA schemes suffer from outage events due to CSIT uncertainties, leading to re-transmissions and increased latency.
skill_point_name: Outage-Free Multi-Layer Multi-Access for Latency and Fairness Enhancement
skill_point_description: Develops a novel non-orthogonal multi-access technique based on multi-layer superposition coding to minimize average queuing latency and enhance fairness under CSIT uncertainties. Each transmitter splits its data into multiple encoded layers, each adapted to a specific combination of all network channel states, preventing outage events. This approach provides closed-form bounds for deterministic arrivals and expressions for Poisson arrivals for average queuing latency. It significantly outperforms single-layer outage approaches by reducing latency growth with increasing arrival rates and improving user fairness, even when users experience weak channel states or strong interference.

problem_description: Ensuring co-existence and interference protection for primary users while enabling opportunistic spectrum access for secondary users FD D2D in heterogeneous networks.
skill_point_name: Integrated System Modeling for Heterogeneous Networks
skill_point_description: Designed, modeled, and evaluated a stochastic geometry model for a Full-Duplex FD enabled Device-to-Device D2D cognitive network. This model rigorously incorporates interference protection for primary users through dynamic guard zones and proposes an optimal mode selection FD, Half-Duplex, or Silent for D2D users based on their proximity to primary user guard zones. The approach critically studies the trade-off between FD gains and induced interference, accounting for imperfect residual self-interference-to-power ratio SIPR.

problem_description: Optimizing D2D communication modes half-duplex, full-duplex, or silent to maximize secondary user capacity while minimizing interference to primary users.
skill_point_name: Dynamic D2D Mode Selection Mechanism
skill_point_description: Developed a novel mechanism for D2D mode selection based on the receiver's vicinity to primary user guard zones. This mechanism ensures that secondary users, SUs, can opportunistically utilize spectrum in either HD or FD modes, provided they adhere to agreed-upon interference protection levels for primary users. This enables a flexible and efficient use of spectrum resources in dynamic spectrum sharing frameworks.

problem_description: Quantifying the performance gains of opportunistic spectrum use with Full-Duplex radios and analyzing the impact of induced interference.
skill_point_name: Performance Quantification and Interference Characterization
skill_point_description: Quantified performance gains for opportunistic spectrum use complemented by FD radios, expressed in terms of the probability of successful receptions for both cellular and D2D users. Utilized expressions for coverage probabilities to provide insights into the impact of different Guard Zone radius values on SU communication. Characterized the induced interference from FD D2D devices and the overall aggregate interference, critically investigating the trade-off between FD operation and spectral efficiency.

problem_description: Analyzing the impact of different LTE transmission techniques on FD D2D performance, especially in unlicensed spectrum coexistence scenarios.
skill_point_name: Coexistence Methodologies Analysis for Multi-RATs
skill_point_description: Evaluated a comparative performance analysis of main coexistence methods for multiple Radio Access Technologies RATs operating in unlicensed spectrum. This includes studying the impact of various LTE transmission techniques continuous, discontinuous transmission, Listen-Before-Talk on FD D2D performance, assessing D2D users' tolerance for aggressive LTE transmissions, and analyzing LTE-unlicensed and WiFi coexistence using duty-cycle based spectrum sharing.

problem_description: Understanding the role of D2D link distance and guard zone stringency on network capacity and interference management.
skill_point_name: Spatial Interference Management and Network Optimization
skill_point_description: Demonstrated through analytical formulations and simulation results that shorter D2D link distances significantly limit the impact of induced interference, thereby allowing for greater frequency reuse in the spatial domain. Thoroughly investigated how varying stringency levels of guard zones influence the capacity of secondary users, highlighting the balance required to optimize overall network performance.

problem_description: Addressing instability of links, frequent network structure changes, energy efficiency, and communication delays in highly mobile vehicular networks.
skill_point_name: SDN-based MEC Enabled Energy-Efficient Resource Scheduling
skill_point_description: Designing and evaluating an approach that integrates Software-Defined Networking and Mobile Edge Computing for energy-efficient resource allocation in IoV. This includes vehicle clustering using Kullback-Leibler Divergence K-Means Algorithm, load balancing with Cumulative Distribution-Satin Bowerbird Optimization, data decomposition using linear decomposition, and vehicle scheduling via Xavier-Convolutional Neural Network classification.

problem_description: Ensuring both security and privacy for communication in IoV systems, particularly against malicious vehicles and attacks like wormhole, blackhole, and false data injection, while minimizing overhead.
skill_point_name: Privacy-Aware Secure Communication with ECC and ACO-AODV
skill_point_description: Developing a secure and privacy-aware communication architecture by mapping vehicle's publicly available information to Elliptic Curve Cryptography ECC keys. This involves a malicious vehicle detection algorithm based on trust levels from periodic status message interactions, and a Secure Optimal Path SOP selection using an improved Ant Colony Optimization Ad hoc On-demand Distance Vector ACO-AODV routing protocol that bypasses untrustworthy vehicles.

problem_description: Detecting malicious entities in highly dynamic Internet of Flying Vehicle IoFV networks, which are vulnerable to attacks like fake ID, replay, interception, and GPS spoofing, and ensuring trusted communication.
skill_point_name: Trust-Based Malicious FV Detection using ECC and Coordinate Information
skill_point_description: Designing a trust-based model for detecting malicious FVs in IoFV communication involves using Certificate Authority CA to map unique FV IDs to ECC cryptographic keys and detecting malicious FVs based on the trustworthiness of received messages, evaluated by distance calculations between FVs and incorporating signal-to-noise ratio to assess message reliability.

problem_description: Enhancing the throughput rate capacity and security of SDN controller-based IoFV networks against cyber-attacks, specifically DDoS attacks, while optimizing FV placement and network paths.
skill_point_name: SDN-enabled Anomaly Detection and Optimal Placement for IoFV with Machine Learning
skill_point_description: Developing an anomaly detection method for IoFV by combining optimal Flying Vehicle FV placement using a Genetic Algorithm, efficient SDN controller placement via Bellman-Ford shortest path algorithm for a single connected graph, and Distributed Denial of Service DDoS attack detection using a Feedforward Neural Network Classifier FNNC trained on features extracted with PCA and LDA.

problem_description: Improving mobility prediction, security, and content caching efficiency in IoV, dealing with dynamic vehicle movements, large sensory data volumes, privacy concerns, and external attacks.
skill_point_name: Mobility-Aware Security and Content Caching with Advanced ML and Crypto
skill_point_description: Proposing an improved Multinomial Recurrent Neural Network MRNN classification technique for accurate vehicle mobility prediction based on features selected by Chaotic Artificial Bird Feeding Optimization CABFO. It also includes content caching optimizing vehicle clustering via Variance Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering Using Hierarchies VBIRCH and relay vehicle selection through Harris Self Avoiding Hawks Optimization HSAHO, and ensuring data security with Caesar Combined Key-ECC 2CK-ECC double encryption.

problem_description: Managing co-channel interference and spectrum reuse while optimizing UAV trajectory, user association, and resource allocation in UAV-based wireless networks.
skill_point_name: Integrated UAV Trajectory Control and Resource Allocation with Co-channel Interference Management
skill_point_description: Developed an alternating optimization approach to solve a mixed-integer non-linear optimization problem for maximizing the min-average rate subject to ground user data demand constraints. Proposed an Iterative Sub-channel Assignment algorithm and utilized Successive Convex Approximation for non-convex UAV trajectory control sub-problems.

problem_description: Maximizing sum rate in Intelligent Reflecting Surface IRS assisted UAV-based wireless networks with wireless access and backhaul links under backhaul capacity constraints.
skill_point_name: UAV Placement and Resource Allocation for IRS-Assisted Wireless Networks
skill_point_description: Derived closed-form solutions for IRS phase shifts and iteratively optimized sub-channel assignment and UAV placement using an alternating optimization method. Applied SCA to convexify and solve the non-convex UAV placement optimization sub-problem, balancing bandwidth allocation for access and backhaul links.

problem_description: Minimizing weighted energy consumption while fulfilling strict delay constraints for computation tasks in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks with complex multi-hop LEO satellite communications.
skill_point_name: Integrated Computation Offloading and Resource Management in SAGIN
skill_point_description: Formulated an optimization problem to jointly optimize partial computation offloading, UAV trajectory control, user scheduling, and resource allocation. Employed an alternating optimization approach and SCA method to address the non-convex MINLP, specifically for computation resource/bandwidth allocation and UAV trajectory control.

problem_description: Ensuring network feasibility and managing overloaded scenarios in SAGIN where resources are limited and task demands vary.
skill_point_name: Feasibility Verification and Admission Control for SAGIN
skill_point_description: Developed efficient strategies for feasibility verification and admission control, including an iterative algorithm for verifying feasibility and a user removal strategy for overloaded network scenarios to satisfy system constraints and maintain service quality.

problem_description: Developing robust and scalable algorithms for complex, non-convex optimization problems in dynamic wireless network environments UAVs, IRS, SAGIN.
skill_point_name: Advanced Optimization and Algorithmic Design
skill_point_description: Proficiently applied advanced mathematical optimization techniques such as Alternating Optimization, Successive Convex Approximation SCA, and Difference of Convex Functions DC programming to derive efficient and converging algorithms for highly complex, non-convex, and mixed-integer non-linear programming MINLP problems. Conducted thorough complexity analysis for proposed algorithms.

problem_description: Maximizing secrecy rate for mobile ground users against static eavesdroppers with limited energy resources for UAVs.
skill_point_name: UAV-Assisted Mobile User Secrecy Optimization
skill_point_description: Developed a practical UAV positioning and multi-user power control scheme to maximize secrecy energy efficiency for efficient and secure multi-user broadband communications. Demonstrated that a single Aerial Relay can significantly improve SEE for a cluster of mobile users, offering a scalable mitigation strategy against distributed eavesdroppers, surpassing traditional base station handover solutions.

problem_description: Optimizing UAV trajectory and transmission power for physical layer security when eavesdropper location is unknown.
skill_point_name: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive UAV Security
skill_point_description: Proposed a Deep Q-Network based reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize the trajectory and transmission power of a UAV acting as an Aerial Base Station to maximize the legitimate channel capacity, thus indirectly improving secrecy capacity, without prior knowledge of the eavesdropper's location. This innovative approach provides a practical solution for real-world deployment challenges where eavesdropper information is typically unavailable.

problem_description: Enhancing physical layer security in multi-user, multi-antenna cellular networks with an AR against passive eavesdropping and unknown Channel State Information.
skill_point_name: Integrated Multi-Antenna Beamforming and UAV Trajectory Optimization
skill_point_description: Designed a comprehensive framework combining machine learning (K-means clustering for user association), deep reinforcement learning (DQN for UAV trajectory), and multi-antenna optimization (WMMSE for GBS, ZF for AR) to maximize the sum-secrecy capacity. This solution effectively addresses multi-user interference and passive eavesdropping by optimizing resource allocation and UAV positioning, demonstrating high scalability and performance even with unknown eavesdropper CSI.

problem_description: Providing on-demand secure wireless coverage and maximizing served users in sparsely connected areas with multiple energy-constrained UAVs under eavesdropping attacks.
skill_point_name: Multi-Agent DRL for Energy-Constrained Secure UAV Coverage
skill_point_description: Introduced a centralized Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient DDPG algorithm on a High-Altitude Platform Station HAPS to coordinate multiple ABSs for optimal trajectory design. This approach intelligently dispatches ABSs to maximize the number of securely served ground users while managing limited on-board energy resources and dynamically adapting to ABS battery depletion, significantly outperforming other learning and baseline methods.

problem_description: Developing mathematical models for various air-to-ground and ground-to-ground channels, including Rician fading and ABG models, to accurately simulate wireless network behavior in the presence of UAVs.
skill_point_name: Advanced Wireless Channel Modeling for UAV Integration
skill_point_description: Proficiently utilized and extended established air-to-ground A2G and ground-to-ground G2G channel models, such as Rician fading for A2G links and the Alpha-Beta-Gamma ABG model for G2G links. This skill underpins the accurate simulation and analysis of complex wireless communication scenarios involving UAVs, enabling robust design and evaluation of physical layer security techniques.

problem_description: The problem of fair computation offloading and resource allocation in MIMO-based MEC systems needs to minimize the maximum weighted consumed energy for mobile users, considering latency and resource limitations under both perfect and imperfect channel state information CSI estimations.
skill_point_name: Optimal and Low-Complexity Computation Offloading in MIMO MEC P-CSI/IP-CSI
skill_point_description: Developed algorithms for optimizing computation offloading and resource allocation in MIMO-based Mobile Edge Computing systems under both perfect P-CSI and imperfect IP-CSI channel state information estimations. For P-CSI, an optimal algorithm using bisection search and decomposition into independent convex subproblems was proposed. For both P-CSI and IP-CSI, low-complexity iterative algorithms were developed by decomposing the problem into offloading optimization OP and power allocation PA subproblems, utilizing Difference of Convex Functions DC programming for non-convex PA in IP-CSI.

problem_description: Jointly optimizing data compression, computation offloading, and resource allocation in hierarchical fog-cloud systems to minimize the maximum weighted energy and service delay cost, considering the computational load incurred by compression/decompression and handling complex problem structures.
skill_point_name: Joint Data Compression and Computation Offloading in Hierarchical Fog-Cloud Systems
skill_point_description: Proposed a non-linear computation model to accurately capture data compression/decompression computational load. Developed an optimal algorithm JCORA for scenarios where data compression occurs only at mobile users, proving optimal offloading decisions have a threshold structure and employing a novel three-step approach with convexification. For the more general case of compression at both mobile users and fog servers, proposed three algorithms: Piece-wise Linear Approximation PLA, One-dimensional Lambda-Search based Two-Stage OSTS, and Iterative Lambda-Update based Two-Stage IUTS to address strong coupling between offloading decisions and resource allocation.

problem_description: Maximizing the number of admitted users while meeting diverse service latency and data transmission requirements in 5G wireless networks with mixed numerology, which is inherently an NP-hard integer programming problem.
skill_point_name: Wireless Scheduling for Heterogeneous Services with Mixed Numerology in 5G Networks
skill_point_description: Studied the scheduling problem for heterogeneous services with mixed numerology, aiming to maximize admitted users under latency and data transmission constraints. Transformed the integer programming problem into an equivalent integer linear program. Developed two low-complexity algorithms: Resource Partitioning-based Algorithm, which divides resources and users into smaller groups for optimized resource allocation and defragmentation, and Iterative Greedy Algorithm, which iteratively assigns resources based on an intelligent weighting scheme to achieve efficient scheduling with low computational complexity.

problem_description: Addressing the complex non-convex and mixed-integer non-linear programming MINLP problems arising from joint optimization of offloading decisions and resource allocation, especially with coupled variables.
skill_point_name: Advanced Optimization Techniques for MINLP Problems
skill_point_description: Applied and developed advanced optimization techniques including bisection search method, decomposition into subproblems, convexification techniques leveraging logarithmic transformations and Difference of Convex Functions programming, and Lagrangian dual methods to effectively solve challenging non-convex and mixed-integer non-linear programming problems in resource management.

problem_description: The need for a robust and adaptable system design that can account for both perfect and imperfect channel state information CSI in dynamic wireless environments, while ensuring fairness among heterogeneous users.
skill_point_name: Robust System Design and Fairness-Aware Resource Management
skill_point_description: Designed resource management algorithms that perform effectively under varying channel conditions, demonstrating adaptability to wireless channel imperfections. Integrated fairness considerations into optimization objectives to ensure equitable resource allocation and performance across diverse mobile users and service requirements.

problem_description: Addressing the challenges of self-interference, spectral inefficiency, and energy inefficiency in full-duplex FD and half-duplex HD communication systems within heterogeneous uplink/downlink macrocells.
skill_point_name: Efficient Signal Transmission and Reception Optimization
skill_point_description: Proposed joint optimization of precoding matrices for base station and uplink users, and optimized time/bandwidth fraction allocation to effectively eliminate self-interference, significantly improving spectral and energy efficiency compared to traditional FD/HD systems.

problem_description: Improving information throughput and secrecy in multi-cell and multi-user energy harvesting scenarios, while managing the inherent complexity of advanced signaling methods.
skill_point_name: Improper Gaussian Signaling for Integrated Data and Energy Networking
skill_point_description: Developed IGS-based beamforming optimization algorithms for energy harvesting networks. Introduced a simplified IGS algorithm with reduced complexity, demonstrating higher user throughput and enhanced information confidentiality compared to conventional Proper Gaussian Signaling based methods.

problem_description: Optimizing Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces RIS and transmit beamforming under the complex non-convex unit-modulus constraint of RIS reflection coefficients, for both Proper and Improper Gaussian Signaling scenarios.
skill_point_name: Joint Design of RIS and Transmit Beamforming with Advanced Signaling
skill_point_description: Devised joint optimization algorithms for RIS phase and transmit beamforming under both PGS and IGS. Introduced a novel method for unit-modulus constraint representation to simplify complexity, showing significant performance gains, especially in scenarios with blocked direct communication paths.

problem_description: Ensuring fairness in user rate allocation and overcoming computational complexity in RIS-aided communication systems, particularly when aiming for geometric mean rate maximization.
skill_point_name: Closed-Form Solution Based GM Rate Maximization for RIS-Aided Networks
skill_point_description: Developed algorithms based on closed-form solutions for efficient GM rate maximization in RIS-aided communication, explicitly balancing edge user throughput and sum rate. Compared PGS and IGS, demonstrating IGS's superior GM rate performance for enhanced rate fairness despite higher computational cost.

problem_description: Integrating RIS-aided communication with energy harvesting, specifically addressing zero-forcing and regularized zero-forcing beamforming for information and energy delivery, and improving information user throughput.
skill_point_name: RIS-Aided ZF/RZF Beamforming for Integrated Information and Energy Delivery
skill_point_description: Proposed joint optimization for information and energy transfer beamforming and time allocation using a transmit time-switching approach. Developed a new RZF beamforming method that significantly improves IU throughput, particularly in scenarios with limited base station antennas, and validated RIS's role in improving IU throughput in EH networks.

problem_description: Traditional obfuscation mechanisms primarily focus on 2D planar areas, leading to impractical outcomes like off-road locations and underestimation of distances in road networks.
skill_point_name: Personalized Road Network-Indistinguishability RN-I and Dual-Obfuscation
skill_point_description: Defined a novel Road Network-Indistinguishability RN-I using route distances to accurately measure indistinguishability in road networks. Developed a Personalized Location Privacy-Preserving PLPP scheme featuring a dual-obfuscation algorithm connection and interval perturbation and a personalization algorithm that tailors privacy budgets based on driver-specified sensitive locations and unique road network features such as connection degrees and route distances. This ensures on-road obfuscation and balances data utility with privacy protection.

problem_description: The additive nature of differential privacy makes detecting illegal trajectories challenging, compromising the utility of location data and quality of Location-Based Services.
skill_point_name: CNN-based Illegal Trajectory Detection
skill_point_description: Proposed a Convolutional Neural Network CNN based detection mechanism to effectively identify illegal trajectories even when drivers protect their actual location data with varying levels of noise. This method operates without requiring the drivers' actual locations, thereby maintaining privacy while ensuring data utility and Quality of Service QoS.

problem_description: Existing obfuscation mechanisms in road networks often ignore the cooperative potential among multiple vehicles to enhance privacy and overlook comprehensive road network features.
skill_point_name: Cloaking Region Obfuscation for Multiple Vehicles
skill_point_description: Designed a Cloaking Region Obfuscation CRO mechanism based on the extended RN-Indistinguishability. This mechanism allows multiple vehicles within the same 'cloaking region' to be uniformly obfuscated, making them indistinguishable from each other. It incorporates various road network features, for example speed limits, road network density, and route distance, to quantify indistinguishability, enabling enhanced cooperative privacy protection in vehicular networks.

problem_description: Previous hybrid mechanisms often process trajectory obfuscation and pseudonym swapping separately, ignoring the temporal dimension and making vehicles vulnerable to long-observation attacks where adversaries link identities over time.
skill_point_name: Joint Trajectory Obfuscation and Pseudonym Swapping JTOPS with Trajectory-Indistinguishability T-I
skill_point_description: Introduced a new unified privacy-preserving measure, Trajectory-Indistinguishability T-I, which quantifies vehicle distinguishability based on historical and current spatial-temporal information. Developed JTOPS, a novel mechanism that jointly employs trajectory obfuscation and pseudonym swapping as a holistic differential privacy process. This mechanism ensures strong location and identity privacy against adversaries with prior knowledge and collusion attacks, crucially demonstrating that pseudonym swaps can be considered a differential privacy process without incurring the additivity composition theorem overhead.

problem_description: Many existing Location Privacy-Preserving Mechanisms LPPMs face limitations in real-world, high-mobility vehicular networks due to high computational complexity, reliance on trusted third parties, or being ill-suited for the dynamic characteristics of road networks.
skill_point_name: Optimized and Practical LPPM Design
skill_point_description: Addressed practical challenges by designing LPPMs with optimized computational and storage efficiency. The PLPP scheme minimizes latency by pre-calculating privacy budgets and perturbation tables. The JTOPS mechanism reduces reliance on trusted third parties by performing local computations for pseudonym swapping. The work consistently emphasizes adapting privacy mechanisms to the unique topological and dynamic features of real-world road networks, moving beyond idealized 2D planar models.

problem_description: Addressing the inherent costs of dynamic offloading, such as decision time, network congestion from decision messages, and performance degradation due to distant offloading, which are often overlooked in existing solutions.
skill_point_name: Hybrid Offloading Algorithm Design
skill_point_description: Developed a novel Hybrid Offloading HybOff algorithm that combines the strengths of static and dynamic offloading approaches. This includes reintroducing static offloading for efficiency, minimizing message exchanges, reducing decision-making time for offloading, encouraging local processing of time-sensitive applications, and efficiently managing networks of all sizes using a cell-based approach. Achieved significant reductions in offloading messages, distance, and decision-offloading consequences, improving load balancing by 97% compared to SOS 64% and DOS 88%.

problem_description: Optimizing service placement in IoT-centric fog environments to reduce latency and network usage for time-sensitive applications, especially in large-scale networks, while acknowledging the limitations of centralized management.
skill_point_name: Reinforcement Optimization for Decentralized Service Placement Policy RODSPP
skill_point_description: Designed 'Reinforcement Optimization for Decentralized Service Placement Policy RODSPP' to enhance load balancing by matching task size with node specifications and prioritizing time-sensitive applications. This decentralized approach reduced service latency by 24.1%, network usage by 4%, and computing usage by 20% compared to existing models by placing computing instances closer to users and intelligently migrating less popular services.

problem_description: Providing a sustainable long-term solution for load balancing in fog computing that can adapt to increasing demand and mitigate the adverse effects of system overload, without relying solely on software-based solutions.
skill_point_name: Sustainable Load Balancing Monitoring System SlbmS
skill_point_description: Developed a 'Sustainable Load Balancing Monitoring System SlbmS' as a comprehensive solution for long-term load balancing. SlbmS collaborates with HybOff, utilizing machine learning Reinforcement Learning and Genetic Algorithms to provide recommendations for physical hardware modifications quality and quantity of Access Points to restore system efficiency in highly congested cells. This approach aims to minimize or eliminate offloading processes by ensuring adequate local physical resources, demonstrating that offloading can be an alternative to traditional resource provisioning.

problem_description: Efficiently managing and categorizing diverse tasks time-sensitive vs. heavy and organizing fog devices into logical clusters to optimize resource allocation and minimize communication overhead.
skill_point_name: Intelligent Task Prioritization and Fog Device Clustering
skill_point_description: Implemented a robust task classification system that prioritizes time-sensitive applications TSA for local execution at edge devices and categorizes heavy applications HA for distributed processing. Utilized the K-means algorithm to form dynamic, contiguous 'cells' of fog devices, improving resource utilization and reducing network traffic by confining inter-device communication within these clusters. This ensures optimal resource allocation based on task urgency and device proximity.

problem_description: Combining elements of centralized and distributed control to achieve both system-wide visibility and local autonomy in managing fog resources, addressing the limitations of solely centralized or distributed approaches.
skill_point_name: Central-Distributed Control System for Resource Management
skill_point_description: Designed and implemented a 'central-distributed control system' where large fog networks are segmented into autonomous mini-controlled systems cells, each governed by an elected master fog server. This hybrid control structure allows for efficient local resource management and offloading within cells, while the master server provides centralized oversight and communication with external systems, enhancing system flexibility, scalability, and reliability by avoiding single points of failure and reducing network bandwidth consumption.

problem_description: Traditional VANET architectures lack flexibility and struggle to efficiently handle increasing data demands, high mobility, and handoffs, leading to performance bottlenecks and high operating expenses.
skill_point_name: Hierarchical 5G VANET Architecture Design
skill_point_description: Developed a novel hierarchical 5G Next-Generation VANET architecture integrating Software Defined Networking, Cloud Radio Access Network, and Fog Computing technologies to enhance flexible network management, control, and resource utilization. This architecture notably improves throughput, reduces transmission delay, and minimizes control overhead on controllers compared to traditional and other 5G VANET architectures.

problem_description: Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks VANETs suffer from cluster instability due to high node mobility, leading to frequent cluster reformation, increased signaling overhead, and reduced routing efficiency.
skill_point_name: Evolutionary Game Theoretic Clustering for VANETs
skill_point_description: Proposed a novel Evolutionary Game Theoretic EGT framework for automated and stable clustering in VANETs. This approach models interactive decision-making among vehicular nodes, uses replicator dynamics to refine clusters and nominate cluster heads, leading to faster convergence, reduced signaling overhead, increased cluster stability, and optimized network throughput. The equilibrium point's existence and stability are analytically proven using Lyapunov function.

problem_description: Meeting diversified Quality of Service demands and dynamic resource requirements in 5G-driven VANETs with fixed resource allocation is inefficient and leads to sub-optimal spectral efficiency and increased operational costs.
skill_point_name: Hybrid Fuzzy Logic Guided Genetic Algorithm H-FLGA for Resource Optimization
skill_point_description: Introduced a Hybrid Fuzzy Logic Guided Genetic Algorithm H-FLGA for the SDN controller to solve multi-objective resource optimization problems in 5G VANETs. This approach dynamically optimizes resource allocation by formulating five network aspects: capacity, delay, number of FC-BBUCs, FC-ZCs per BBUC, traffic load; and using a Fuzzy Inference System FIS to adaptively assign weights based on Type of Service ToS requirements, resulting in improved spectral efficiency, reduced End-to-End delay, and lower OpEx.

problem_description: Accommodating high volumes of mission-critical traffic in 5G VANETs while guaranteeing ultra-reliability and low latency, without over-provisioning resources, is a significant challenge.
skill_point_name: End-to-End Network Slicing Framework
skill_point_description: Developed an E2E network slicing framework for 5G-driven VANETs to achieve customized QoS provisioning for mixed traffic, best-effort and mission-critical. This framework manages cooperation between the Radio Access Network RAN and Core Network CN using SDN, NFV, and Edge Computing, dynamically optimizing radio resource slices using a Genetic Algorithm. This ensures precise resource allocation, meeting stringent KPIs like ultra-reliability and low E2E latency for mission-critical services.

problem_description: Conventional networks struggle with dynamic customer needs and capacity fluctuations, leading to inflexible infrastructure and difficulties in adopting new services efficiently.
skill_point_name: Customer-Centric Network Infrastructure Design
skill_point_description: Enabled the implementation of a more flexible, customer-centric network infrastructure for service providers. This is achieved through the integration of 5G-driven technologies SDN, C-RAN, NFV, Fog/Edge Computing and optimized resource allocation strategies H-FLGA, E2E Network Slicing, allowing the network to automatically adapt to dynamic customer needs and capacity demand fluctuations, thereby reducing both operating and capital expenses.

problem_description: Wireless communication systems face significant challenges in signal synchronization, particularly with large carrier frequency offsets, affecting high-speed aerial backbone links.
skill_point_name: Low-Complexity Synchronization with Large CFO
skill_point_description: Developed an effective, low-complexity method for signal synchronization in high-speed wireless communication, capable of real-time Carrier Frequency Offset estimation and compensation. This method integrates CFO estimation with autocorrelation operation, where initial CFO estimation accuracy gradually improves as autocorrelation proceeds. Optimized implementation ensures low resource usage on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays while effectively capturing and compensating for tens of MHz CFO, demonstrating minimal performance loss compared to systems without CFO.

problem_description: High-speed wideband wireless communication systems suffer from In-phase/Quadrature-phase imbalance and require complex, resource-intensive digital signal processing for compensation, channel equalization, and sample rate conversion.
skill_point_name: Joint I/Q Compensation, Channel Equalization, and SRC
skill_point_description: Proposed a low-complexity and effective serial method at the receiver for estimating and compensating both Receiver Rx and Transmitter Tx I/Q imbalances. The method involves designing a training sequence for efficient channel and Tx I/Q imbalance estimation, estimating Rx I/Q imbalance based on received signal statistical properties in presence of CFO and compensating it with a time-domain linear filter, and then jointly estimating channel and Tx I/Q imbalance using the compensated training sequence. This joint algorithm effectively combines channel equalization and sample rate conversion, significantly reducing digital signal processing cost and increasing data rate for wideband systems.

problem_description: Achieving high data rates in wireless communications is limited by the availability and cost of high-sampling-rate Analog-to-Digital and Digital-to-Analog converters.
skill_point_name: Dual Pulse Shaping Transmission Technique
skill_point_description: Introduced a novel Dual Pulse Shaping DPS transmission scheme that allows the use of half-symbol-rate D/A and A/D devices to achieve full Nyquist rate transmission. This is accomplished by splitting data symbols into two half-rate data streams, each passed through a respective pulse shaping filter. The method incorporates complementary Nyquist pulses to satisfy a Cross-Symbol Interference CSI-free condition, enabling spectral overlap without interference. Low-complexity Zero-Forcing ZF and Minimum Mean Square Error MMSE equalization techniques are specifically tailored for DPS, offering a practical and cost-effective solution for high-speed communications, especially when very high sampling-rate conversion devices are unattainable or too costly.

problem_description: Implementing high-speed, wideband wireless communication systems in real-time, especially on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays, faces challenges in optimizing resource usage, meeting strict timing constraints, and handling large data throughputs.
skill_point_name: High-Speed Digital Modem Real-Time Implementation on FPGA
skill_point_description: Successfully implemented a 20 Gbps high-speed digital modem in real-time on an FPGA platform. This involved designing optimized architectures for Ethernet interfaces, transmitter Tx and receiver Rx filters, and other signal processing modules encoding, modulation, synchronization, channel estimation/equalization, demodulation, decoding. Key strategies were developed for FPGA implementation to achieve low resource usage and meet high-speed system clock timing constraints, including wide word-length addition operations, efficient memory utilization BRAM vs. Distributed RAM, resource sharing, optimized precision for algorithms, and avoidance of huge data storage. Experimental results validated the modem's performance and its integration with IF modules and a THz RF frontend.

problem_description: Practical wideband wireless systems often exhibit undesirable hardware impairments, such as significant frequency response fluctuations and I/Q imbalance, necessitating robust compensation techniques.
skill_point_name: Channel Pre-equalization for Wideband Systems
skill_point_description: Proposed and implemented channel pre-equalization as an effective strategy to mitigate the influence of hardware impairments, particularly significant fluctuations in the channel frequency responses of Intermediate Frequency IF modules in wideband systems. By applying pre-equalization, the characteristics of the signal transmitted via the IF module are significantly altered at the transmitter, for example, changing the real and imaginary parts of Tx filters, which in turn transforms the effective channel impulse response at the receiver to be shorter and more concentrated.
