skill_point_description: Successfully developed and characterized freestanding thin-film TiNiCuCo superelastic alloys structured into serpentine geometries for stretchable electrical interconnects. Demonstrated their ability to achieve significantly larger elastic elongations 5X-7X compared to copper, while maintaining stable electrical resistance under large deformation. This involved experimental fabrication, tensile testing, electrical resistance measurements, and detailed finite element analysis FEA.

problem_description: Magnetoelectric sensors often require tunable resonant frequencies for specific applications like biomagnetic diagnostics.
skill_point_name: Integration of SMAs for Tunable Resonant Frequency Sensors
skill_point_description: Developed a MEMS-based fabrication route to integrate AlN piezoelectric thin films on ultralow fatigue TiNiCu shape memory alloys for magnetoelectric sensors. Demonstrated analytically and experimentally how the thermal-induced phase transformation in SMA can be used to tune the mechanical resonance frequency of the sensor, achieving high sensitivity. This involved careful process optimization to ensure high-quality AlN deposition and prevent interdiffusion at interfaces.

problem_description: Micro and nano-actuators need to operate reliably with large displacements and potentially bistable states, especially when downscaled.
skill_point_name: Design and Characterization of SMA-based Micro/Nano Actuators
skill_point_description: Researched and developed TiNiHf/SiO₂/Si shape memory film composites for bi-directional and bistable micro/nano actuation. Investigated the influence of film thickness and substrate on phase transformation properties, showing that TiNiHf films as thin as 220nm can display high-temperature actuation. Utilized constitutional modeling to predict optimal thickness combinations for achieving bistable actuation in PMMA/TiNiHf/Si trimorph composites.

problem_description: Conventional auxetic structures have limited expandability/compressibility and may not be suitable for demanding medical or wearable applications.
skill_point_name: Innovation of Stretchable Auxetic Geometries with SMAs
skill_point_description: Introduced novel stretchable auxetic geometries, 'rotating serpentine rectangle' and 'rotating archimedean rectangle,' fabricated with superelastic TiNiCuCo thin films. Demonstrated enhanced stretchability and compressibility compared to traditional auxetic structures, retaining auxetic behavior under large axial strains. Showcased the ability to shape-set these 2D films into complex 3D structures for medical device applications like spheres and cylinders.

problem_description: Achieving highly fatigue-resistant thin-film SMAs, especially when scaled to micro/nano dimensions, is challenging.
skill_point_name: Advanced Fabrication and Microstructure Control for Ultra-low Fatigue SMAs
skill_point_description: Mastered DC magnetron sputter deposition and rapid thermal annealing to precisely control the composition and microstructure of NiTi-based SMA thin-films TiNiCu, TiNiCuCo, TiNiHf. Demonstrated synthesis of ultra-low fatigue SMAs capable of millions of cycles without degradation, linking annealing parameters to microstructure and functional/structural fatigue properties. This skill is foundational to enabling the other MEMS applications.

problem_description: Manufacturing challenges leading to low yield and variability in Harvard Ambulatory Microrobot HAMR fabrication, especially for small-scale versions.
skill_point_name: Robust Microrobot Fabrication at Scale
skill_point_description: Improved and streamlined HAMR manufacturing processes, including material assessment, laser cutting adjustments, pre-cut layer leveling, consistent cleanliness, and strategic use of adhesives. This enabled reliable fabrication of the 2 cm HAMR-JR microrobot with 90-100% actuator yield, making complex microrobot production more efficient and consistent.

problem_description: Limited adhesion strength and payload capacity of microrobots on pristine, smooth surfaces given fixed robot size and material constraints.
skill_point_name: Enhanced Electroadhesion for Pristine Surfaces
skill_point_description: Explored design parameters and refined fabrication of unipolar electroadhesive pads, specifically reducing dielectric layer thickness through multi-layer lamination of 7.5 µm Kapton. Achieved significantly improved shear force, up to 60 g at 700V, demonstrating a high factor of safety for carrying substantial payloads relevant for autonomous microrobots.

problem_description: Decreased adhesion force and locomotion capability of microrobots on rough and inclined surfaces due to air gaps reducing effective contact area.
skill_point_name: Compliant Electroadhesive Design for Rough Terrains
skill_point_description: Developed and characterized compliant electroadhesive pad designs, specifically 'spoked' and 'serpentine' geometries, to increase local conformance to surface heterogeneities. Demonstrated enhanced shear adhesion forces and improved robot locomotion over steep inclines, up to 37 degrees on rough surfaces, significantly outperforming standard circular pads.

problem_description: Lack of quantitative understanding of how specific geometric parameters in kirigami patterns affect the compliance and adhesion performance of electroadhesive pads on rough surfaces.
skill_point_name: Kirigami-Inspired Compliance Modeling and Design
skill_point_description: Conducted a detailed design exploration of various kirigami geometries spokes, serpentine, fractal patterns for electroadhesive pads, developing a simple bending beam model for spoke design parameters. Identified serpentine designs as most effective for enhancing compliance and shear adhesion capability on rough surfaces up to twice the adhesion force of circular designs, linking geometric features to performance.

problem_description: Microrobots' inability to effectively interact with and manipulate objects in real-world environments.
skill_point_name: Electroadhesive Gripping and Manipulation Strategy
skill_point_description: Demonstrated the potential for integrating compliant electroadhesive pads into gripping and manipulation applications for microrobots. Showcased the ability to manipulate irregularly shaped convex/concave and textured conductive objects, highlighting electroadhesion as a robust and adaptable alternative to traditional grippers, even for ungrounded objects with the addition of grounding prongs.

problem_description: The complex dynamics and high modal density of bladed structures make vibration mitigation challenging, particularly when multiple, closely-spaced modes need to be damped simultaneously.
skill_point_name: Multimodal Vibration Mitigation with Multiple Digital Vibration Absorbers DVAs
skill_point_description: Developed and experimentally validated a damping concept utilizing multiple Digital Vibration Absorbers DVAs simultaneously. Introduced two novel tuning strategies, 'isolated mode' and 'mean shunt', to effectively address the complex dynamics and high modal density of bladed structures. These strategies leverage the simultaneous action of multiple absorbers and are robust to closely-spaced modes and mistuning.

problem_description: Traditional analog piezoelectric shunt circuits are often bulky, difficult to tune, and limited in their ability to target low frequencies due to the need for impractically large inductances.
skill_point_name: Digital Realization of Piezoelectric Shunt Circuits
skill_point_description: Designed and implemented piezoelectric Digital Vibration Absorbers DVAs that digitally synthesize the entire shunt impedance. This digital approach eliminates the need for bulky analog components, allows for easy adjustability of shunt parameters to adapt to mistuning or changes in the host structure, and is compact, especially when implemented on Printed Circuit Boards PCBs.

problem_description: Digital control systems inherently introduce sampling delays, for example, due to Zero-Order Hold - ZOH, that can lead to instabilities in the controlled system if not properly accounted for during discretization.
skill_point_name: Novel Discretization Procedure for Digital Shunt Admittance
skill_point_description: Proposed and validated a novel discretization procedure for the shunt admittance that directly considers the ZOH discretization of the plant transfer function. This method ensures that the poles of the discrete closed-loop transfer function are the discrete equivalent of the continuous one, thereby preventing delay-induced instabilities and preserving closed-loop stability, even at high frequencies or with large sampling periods.

problem_description: Identifying the dynamic characteristics of complex structures like bladed assemblies for accurate shunt tuning can be challenging, often requiring numerical models or complex experimental setups.
skill_point_name: Experimental Identification and Tuning Based on Measured Dynamic Impedances
skill_point_description: Developed a practical procedure for shunt tuning that relies solely on experimental measurements of dynamic impedance functions using multiple DVAs. Applied advanced system identification methods PolyMAX to extract critical system parameters resonance frequencies, damping ratios, DVA imperfections directly from measured data, eliminating the need for a numerical model of the host structure and greatly facilitating the application of the method.

problem_description: While passive shunt circuits are stable, active control methods like Positive Position Feedback controllers offer enhanced control authority but pose challenges for stability and optimal tuning, particularly when considering the influence of multiple modes.
skill_point_name: Unified H-infinity Tuning Rule for Active and Passive Vibration Controllers
skill_point_description: Established a theoretical parallel between resonant piezoelectric shunts with negative capacitance NCRL shunts and active Positive Position Feedback PPF controllers, demonstrating an equivalence in their receptance functions and control parameters. Derived an exact H-infinity norm-based tuning rule for PPF controllers, providing a closed-form expression for optimal performance. Extended this rule to the multi-degree-of-freedom MDOF case by developing a correction procedure that accounts for the influence of higher-order modes, significantly improving damping effectiveness and stability margins in practical applications.

problem_description: Traditional fiber fabrication methods are limited in creating complex geometries and integrating diverse materials. This limits the functionality and application range of smart fibers.
skill_point_name: Very Large Scale Integration for Fibers VLSI-Fi Technology
skill_point_description: VLSI-Fi is an innovative fabrication technique inspired by microelectronics manufacturing principles. It combines 3D printing for preform components, thermal drawing to transform assembled preforms into fibers, and post-draw processes like material-selective spatially coherent capillary breakup and etching to shape integrated devices within the fibers. This '2D+1D+0D' strategy enables precise control over fiber architecture and functionalities, integrating diverse materials like semiconductors, metals, polymers, and glasses.

problem_description: Developing complex multimaterial fiber devices is time-consuming and costly, often requiring numerous physical drawing attempts to optimize material selection, assembly, and testing parameters.
skill_point_name: Systematic Multimaterial Fiber Device Design Process with Integrated Life Cycle Assessment LCA
skill_point_description: A tailored step-by-step design process specifically for multimaterial fiber devices in biomedical applications. This process integrates problem definition, needs identification, information gathering, concept generation, concept selection, embodiment & detail design including CAD/CAE simulations, material flow & prototype creation, device evaluation & testing, and iterative refinement. Crucially, it incorporates Life Cycle Assessment at each relevant step to ensure environmental sustainability, reduce errors, and streamline development, minimizing prototyping attempts.

problem_description: Predicting and controlling the flow behavior of multimaterial polymers during thermal drawing is crucial for consistent fiber quality and preventing defects, but often relies on empirical trials.
skill_point_name: Advanced Rheological Characterization for Polymer Fiber Drawing
skill_point_description: Utilizing rheology measurements to quantify the flow and deformation behavior of multimaterial polymers at different temperatures. This includes characterizing viscoelastic properties, storage modulus, loss modulus, and phase-shift angle, and dynamic viscosity. By comparing rheology data with thermal conditions in the draw tower furnace and incorporating corrections for heat transfer delays, this skill enables accurate prediction of drawing conditions, optimizing material selection for compatible viscosities, and reducing the need for extensive trial-and-error.

problem_description: Creating functional microstructures, for example, arrays of spheres and micro-windows, within fibers requires precise control over material breakup and selective removal, which is challenging to achieve consistently.
skill_point_name: Controlled Capillary Breakup and Selective Etching for In-Fiber Device Patterning
skill_point_description: Mastery of inducing and controlling capillary breakup in cylindrical fiber cores, both through uniform and non-uniform heating, to transform continuous cores into periodic arrays of discrete spheres. This involves understanding the underlying physics Tomotika model and precisely managing temperature, tension, and feed speeds. Subsequently, selective chemical etching processes are employed to partially remove cladding or core materials, creating micro-windows or exposing functional elements like metallic microwires, enabling the precise patterning and integration of miniature components within the fiber.

problem_description: Current approaches to tissue engineering and medical device testing often rely on animal models or simplified in-vitro systems that lack physiological realism or offer limited analytical feedback.
skill_point_name: Development of Physiologically Realistic 3D Bioprinted Models and Integrated Fiber Devices for Biomedical Research
skill_point_description: Expertise in designing and fabricating complex 3D bioprinted anatomical models, such as gut bioreactors and TrophoWell tissue engineering platforms, that accurately mimic multi-scale physiological features and fluid dynamics. This includes utilizing advanced additive manufacturing techniques like stereolithography and Digital Light Processing for precise geometries. Furthermore, the skill involves conceptualizing and integrating functional fiber devices, for vascularization, drug delivery, and sensing, within these bioprinted constructs to enable real-time monitoring, controlled environmental manipulation, and more physiologically relevant experimental setups, providing alternatives to traditional animal studies.

problem_description: Quantifying the relative fractions of piezoelectric crystal phases beta and gamma in PVDF is challenging due to overlapping spectral features in traditional analysis.
skill_point_name: Fourier Self-Deconvolution for PVDF Phase Quantification
skill_point_description: Developed and applied an innovative Fourier Self-Deconvolution FSD method to FTIR spectra, specifically for the 840 cm-1 peak, to accurately resolve and quantify the relative and absolute fractions of beta and gamma phases in PVDF electrospun fibers and electrosprayed films. This method synthetically narrows broad and complex infrared absorbance spectra, significantly enhancing resolution and providing reliable quantitative analysis.

problem_description: Membrane fouling is a major issue in filtration, increasing operational costs and environmental pollution, while maintaining inherent hydrophobicity is crucial for certain applications.
skill_point_name: Fouling-Resistant Hydrophobic Electrospun Membranes
skill_point_description: Fabricated novel fouling-resistant non-woven fibrous membranes by electrospinning blended solutions of PVDF with a newly synthesized polyampholytic copolymer r-PAC. The r-PAC, being amphiphilic, enhances fouling resistance by forming a strong hydration shell while preserving PVDF's inherent hydrophobicity, demonstrating a balance between anti-fouling properties and water-repellency for oil-water separation.

problem_description: Processing PVDF typically involves hazardous solvents DMAc, DMF, NMP that pose significant health and environmental risks.
skill_point_name: Sustainable PVDF Processing with Green Solvents
skill_point_description: Investigated and successfully demonstrated the use of gamma-valerolactone GVL, a low-toxic and biorenewable solvent, for electrospinning PVDF solutions. Addressed the challenge of rapid sol-to-gel transition in PVDF/GVL solutions through comprehensive oscillatory rheological analysis, identifying optimal temperature and shear rate conditions, and demonstrating successful nanoscale fiber formation with LiCl as an additive. This innovation offers a greener alternative to traditional hazardous solvents in PVDF manufacturing.

problem_description: Characterizing the complex multi-step thermal degradation patterns of novel polyampholytes and understanding their glass-forming ability for high-temperature applications.
skill_point_name: Advanced Thermal Degradation and Glass Transition Analysis
skill_point_description: Performed detailed thermogravimetric analysis TGA to delineate complex multi-step thermal degradation processes of novel polyampholyte variants, confirming sequential degradation of specific monomer units MAETA, TFEMA, MAA. Utilized Fast Scanning Calorimetry FSC to accurately determine glass transition temperatures and dynamic fragility indices, providing crucial insights into the glass-forming behavior and operational temperature limits of these new polymers, particularly their ability to form moderately strong glasses.

problem_description: Ensuring high-quality electrospun fiber morphology and optimizing process parameters is challenging due to the complex interplay of solution and processing variables.
skill_point_name: High-Resolution Morphological and Process Optimization
skill_point_description: Employed high-resolution Scanning Electron Microscopy SEM coupled with advanced image analysis software DiameterJ to meticulously characterize and quantify fiber diameters and porosity in electrospun mats. Systematically optimized electrospinning parameters voltage, working distance, pump rate and solution properties viscosity, concentration, conductivity to control fiber morphology, including bead formation, and achieve desired nanoscale fiber diameters for specific applications like filtration.

problem_description: Precise control over the structure, growth, and properties of 2D/3D interfaces is challenging due to phenomena like temperature effects, defects, surface reconstructions, and interface chemistry influencing morphology, and the difficulty in obtaining atomically clean surfaces.
skill_point_name: Atomic-Scale Interface Control and Characterization
skill_point_description: Developed methods for achieving epitaxial, faceted 2D/3D interfaces with ultra-low defect densities, including meticulous substrate preparation 2D material transfer to TEM grids and UHV annealing for surface cleanliness. Quantitatively estimated quasi-vdW interface energy using thermodynamic modeling of equilibrium island shapes on various 2D materials. This includes understanding the influence of surface chemistry, reconstructions, and substrate defects on nucleation density and island morphology. Demonstrated precise control of growth parameters temperature, flux rate to achieve desired nanostructure morphology e.g., transition from dendritic to compact shapes.

problem_description: Understanding the complex interplay between atomic structure and local electronic/excitonic properties at 2D/3D interfaces, especially in the presence of moiré superlattices and projection artifacts in conventional imaging techniques.
skill_point_name: Moire Engineering and Electronic Property Mapping
skill_point_description: Demonstrated the use of advanced STEM techniques iDPC and 4D STEM combined with a geometric convolution technique to decouple and directly image higher-order moiré patterns at the 2D/3D interface, resolving discrepancies between conventional imaging methods. Utilized ab initio electronic structure calculations to show how moiré periodicity modulates charge density at the interface, providing a direct link between atomic structure and electronic modulation. Conducted correlative EELS and nanoARPES measurements to identify and explain excitonic peaks related to dielectric screening at the 2D/3D interface, showcasing the ability to map local optoelectronic property variations with nanoscale resolution.

problem_description: Achieving selective synthesis of chiral nanostructures with high crystallinity and enantiomeric selectivity, which is challenging via solid-state synthesis methods.
skill_point_name: Chiral Epitaxy and Kinetic Mechanism Elucidation
skill_point_description: Discovered and elucidated a novel form of van der Waals epitaxy, 'chiral epitaxy,' demonstrating that the chiral surface structure of ReSe2 can template a >70% enantiomeric selectivity for tellurium nanoribbons. Used in situ environmental TEM ETEM with MBE deposition sources to directly observe nucleation and growth, determining that chirality is primarily nucleation-driven rather than growth-driven. Quantified the influence of substrate, temperature, and flux rate on the resulting interface, estimating activation energies for nucleation and diffusion distances, which provides fundamental design rules for chiral vdW epitaxy.

problem_description: Controlling the formation of technologically relevant 2D/3D oxide interfaces, as conventional oxidation methods often lead to uneven and non-conformal oxide layers due to material volatility.
skill_point_name: Controlled Oxide Interface Formation
skill_point_description: Investigated atomic-scale oxidation mechanisms of MoS2, identifying that thermal oxidation proceeds via vapor-phase mass transport and redeposition, resulting in crystalline α-MoO3 with sharp interfaces but uneven morphology. Proposed and demonstrated that non-thermal methods like oxygen plasma processing can produce smooth, conformal, amorphous MoO3 layers via a kinetically-limited oxidize-in-place mechanism. This provides quantitative guidance for managing both atomic-scale structure and thin-film morphology of oxides in TMD device design.

problem_description: Controlling the growth and properties of complex mixed-dimensional heterostructures for advanced devices, including managing defect formation, strain, and achieving site-selective deposition.
skill_point_name: Complex Heterostructure Fabrication and Tailoring
skill_point_description: Explored the effect of defects, dislocations, and strain on 2D/3D interface growth, particularly in the Ti/Graphene system, identifying a thickness-dependent dislocation formation related to graphene compliance. Demonstrated the fabrication of 3D/2D/3D structures and showed the ability to tailor growth locations using defect sites or strain fields. Fabricated ultrathin multi-element lateral and vertical heterostructures, for example, Au/Ti on Gr, Si/Ge via metal catalysis, illustrating the transfer of epitaxy and high selectivity of deposition, relevant for future technological integration including contact adhesion, thermal stability, and catalytically mediated epitaxy for semiconductor growth.

problem_description: Cooling a continuum of traveling-wave phonons in macroscopic media like optical fibers previously faced challenges due to weak light-sound coupling and short phonon lifetimes.
skill_point_name: Laser Cooling of Traveling-Wave Phonons in Optical Fiber
skill_point_description: Demonstrated the first instance of laser cooling a continuum of traveling-wave phonons in a liquid-core optical fiber by leveraging anti-Stokes Brillouin scattering. Achieved significant phonon population reduction exceeding 20K effective temperature reduction under ambient conditions, extending optomechanical cooling beyond chip-scale systems to meter-scale fibers and enabling new low-noise acousto-optic technologies.

problem_description: Traditional Brillouin scattering spectrometers suffer from low sensitivity, especially for short, low-gain samples, and strict phase-matching requirements.
skill_point_name: Coherently Stimulated Brillouin Spectrometer
skill_point_description: Developed a novel four-wave mixing spectrometer (pump, probe, driven Stokes, observed signal) that dramatically improves sensitivity (sub-10fW) for phonon spectroscopy. By relaxing traditional phase-matching constraints, CoBS achieves a 10^6 increase in scattered power over mm- to cm-scale lengths, enabling analyses of ultrathin-films and microfluidic samples previously inaccessible to Brillouin methods.

problem_description: The distinction between traveling-wave Brillouin phonons and standing-wave Raman-like modes is often blurred in confined systems, suggesting a potential for unifying these phenomena but requiring specific conditions.
skill_point_name: Exploration of Brillouin-Induced Raman Modes
skill_point_description: Investigated theoretical and experimental conditions for observing Brillouin-induced Raman-like modes at room temperature. Explored various material platforms, for example Ge-doped fiber, liquid CS2, TeO2/Te thin films, suspended waveguides, to systematically study the transition from continuous Brillouin scattering to discrete standing-wave vibrational modes, aiming to bridge the Brillouin and Raman paradigms of light-sound interaction.

problem_description: The presence of asymmetric spectral line shapes, Fano resonances, in small-signal Brillouin measurements complicates accurate parameter extraction when conventional Lorentzian fits are used.
skill_point_name: Fano-Resonant Asymmetry Analysis in CoBS
skill_point_description: Identified and quantitatively characterized Fano-resonant asymmetries observed in CoBS measurements, especially at low signal levels. Demonstrated the superiority of Fano function fits over Lorentzian fits for accurately extracting spectral parameters such as linewidth, resonant frequency, and peak amplitude, and suggested methods for dynamic phase-relationship tuning to potentially 'boost' weak signals or control line shape.

problem_description: Lack of a standardized metric for laser cooling performance makes comparisons across different systems and initial temperatures misleading.
skill_point_name: Standardized Cooling Metric C-Value
skill_point_description: Proposed a new standardized cooling metric, the 'C-value', expressed as a percentage of degrees cooled relative to the initial temperature. This metric offers greater transparency, clarity, and universal applicability for comparing cooling techniques across diverse optomechanical systems and application fields, overcoming the limitations of reporting only absolute temperature reduction.

problem_description: Existing shape sensing methods photogrammetry, accelerometry, iFEM are limited by environmental conditions, optical access, or computational cost, especially in harsh or dynamic environments.
skill_point_name: Kinematic Shape Sensor KSS Design and Reconstruction
skill_point_description: Developed a Kinematic Shape Sensor KSS using strategically placed strain gauges and a robust kinematic model. This method reconstructs 3D deflections bi-axial bending and torsion in real-time 5000-8000Hz, is computationally inexpensive, and overcomes limitations of optical access or static deformation measurement.

problem_description: Previous kinematic models assumed small deformations and were subject to large errors in torsion calculations due to error propagation from bending precision errors.
skill_point_name: Revised Kinematic Model for Large Deformations
skill_point_description: Proposed a revised kinematic model that removes the small deformation assumption and improves torsion calculation accuracy. This model uses multiple coordinate systems global, spar-aligned, bending-aligned and forward Euler integration to accurately reconstruct large deformations, addressing a significant limitation of prior models.

problem_description: Accurate parameter estimation in complex fluid-structure interaction FSI systems is challenging, especially with output-only data and non-stationary, non-Gaussian inputs.
skill_point_name: Output-Only Parameter Estimation with SSI-COV
skill_point_description: Validated the use of the Covariance Driven Stochastic Subspace Identification SSI-COV algorithm with KSS data for accurate and robust output-only parameter estimation. Demonstrated its effectiveness in identifying natural frequencies, damping ratios, and mode shapes across various noise types and single-frequency contaminants, outperforming other methods in computational cost and user input.

problem_description: Distinguishing between structural resonances and periodically forced vibrations in FSI data, especially when input forces are unknown, is difficult.
skill_point_name: Fluid-Structure Co-analysis Method
skill_point_description: Developed a novel co-analysis framework that combines SSI-COV for structural response with Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition SPOD applied to high-speed video data of the flow. This method disambiguates structural resonances from coherent forcing events, for example, vortex shedding, fan blade passage, providing deeper insight into FSI mechanisms.

problem_description: Understanding hydroelastic effects in complex multiphase flows ventilation, cavitation, waves and their impact on structural dynamics in real-world scenarios is crucial but difficult to measure.
skill_point_name: In-situ FSI Characterization in Multiphase Flows
skill_point_description: Applied the KSS and the co-analysis method to characterize the hydroelastic response of a surface-piercing hydrofoil in multiphase flows ventilation, cavitation, waves. Demonstrated the KSS's ability to measure static hydrodynamic loading, identify phenomena like modal coalescence, mode switching, and wave modulation, and relate these to fluid mechanisms, providing invaluable insight into complex FSI processes.

problem_description: Traditional depth sensing struggles with transparent and specular objects, hindering robotic grasping performance.
skill_point_name: Multi-modal Transfer Learning for Transparent/Specular Object Grasping
skill_point_description: Devised a transfer learning method leveraging cross-modal network distillation to enable RGB-based grasping of transparent and specular objects by transferring knowledge from a pre-trained depth-based grasp network. This approach avoids the need for ground-truth grasp success labels or real grasp attempts.

problem_description: Current 6-DOF grasp estimation methods produce discrete grasp sets, leading to brittle, multi-stage pipelines for grasp and motion planning.
skill_point_name: Neural Grasp Distance Fields NGDF for Joint Grasp and Motion Planning
skill_point_description: Introduced Neural Grasp Distance Fields, a neural implicit function representing the continuous manifold of valid 6-DOF grasp poses. This allows for joint optimization of grasping and reaching motions within a single optimization framework by interpreting grasp distance as a cost, significantly outperforming discrete methods.

problem_description: Manipulating deformable cloth requires identifying specific regions distinct from wrinkles/folds and determining precise grasp directions.
skill_point_name: Cloth Region Segmentation and Grasp Direction Estimation
skill_point_description: Developed a method for segmenting true edges and corners of cloth from depth images, distinguishing them from wrinkles. It also provides an algorithm to estimate the grasp location, direction, and directional uncertainty, enabling robust grasping of crumpled cloth configurations.

problem_description: Vision-only approaches are often insufficient for fine-grained cloth manipulation tasks, such as grasping a specific number of cloth layers from a stack due to high uncertainty.
skill_point_name: Tactile Feedback for Precise Cloth Layer Singulation
skill_point_description: Implemented a closed-loop tactile sensing policy using a magnetometer-based ReSkin sensor. This policy accurately determines the number of cloth layers grasped and adjusts the gripper height through a classifier, outperforming image-based methods in robustness and generalization for singulating cloth layers.

problem_description: Goal-conditioned cloth manipulation is challenging due to cloth deformability and the need for complex, often bimanual, actions; existing methods struggle with generalizability and efficient action representation.
skill_point_name: FabricFlowNet for Bimanual Cloth Folding via Flow-based Policy
skill_point_description: Proposed FabricFlowNet FFN, a novel policy that leverages optical flow as both an input and an action representation for goal-conditioned bimanual cloth folding. FFN learns to predict pick points and uses the flow to determine place points, enabling elegant switching between dual-arm and single-arm actions and demonstrating strong sim-to-real transfer and generalization to unseen cloth shapes.

problem_description: Traditional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability HJR analysis suffers from the 'curse of dimensionality' for high-dimensional systems and does not guarantee stabilizability after reaching a goal.
skill_point_name: Robust Control Lyapunov-Value Function R-CLVF
skill_point_description: Introduces R-CLVF, a Lipschitz continuous function computable via numerical tools from HJR analysis. It exponentially stabilizes nonlinear systems with bounded control and disturbance to an arbitrary point of interest's Smallest Robust Control Invariant Set, providing a theoretical foundation for practical stabilization in infinite-time horizons.

problem_description: The 'curse of dimensionality' makes HJR-based methods computationally prohibitive for high-dimensional systems, such as those with 6D or more.
skill_point_name: Refined Self-Contained Subsystem Decomposition with Admissible Control Sets
skill_point_description: Develops a refined decomposition framework using Admissible Control Sets ACS to address the 'curse of dimensionality' in HJR and R-CLVF computations. This method significantly improves approximation quality by mitigating the 'leaking corner problem' caused by shared controls and inexact target decomposition, enabling efficient analysis of high-dimensional systems.

problem_description: Combining multiple objectives reach, avoid, and stay/stabilize in a single unified framework for autonomous systems is challenging, especially with disturbances and multiple targets/obstacles.
skill_point_name: Multi-Objective Reach-Avoid-Stay RAS Problem Solution via ACS and New Value Function
skill_point_description: Presents two novel approaches to the Reach-Avoid-Stay RAS problem: one leveraging the ACS concept from system decomposition to manage multiple goals and obstacles sequentially, and another introducing a new discounted HJR value function that unifies reach-avoid and stabilize-avoid objectives into a single computation, suitable for continuous-time nonlinear systems.

problem_description: Autonomous navigation systems often struggle with unexpected unmodeled disturbances and optimizing navigation speed in unknown environments while ensuring safety.
skill_point_name: Safe Returning FaSTrack SR-F for Unmodeled Disturbances
skill_point_description: Modifies the FaSTrack framework to develop SR-F, which uses R-CLVF to guarantee that the tracking error bound TEB can return safely to its nominal state after experiencing unexpected, unmodeled disturbances. This framework also enables accelerated navigation by intentionally 'jumping' the planner forward in obstacle-free environments.

problem_description: Fixed control bounds in navigation frameworks like FaSTrack lead to either conservative movement in open spaces or unsafe behavior in cluttered environments.
skill_point_name: Parametric FaSTrack for Adaptive Navigation Speed
skill_point_description: Introduces P-F, a modification of FaSTrack that dynamically adapts the planner's control bounds based on the sensed environment using DeepReach's parameter-conditioned reachability. This allows for intelligent trade-offs between safety and efficiency, enabling higher speeds in open environments and slower, safer movements in narrow or cluttered areas.

problem_description: DAS data contains high levels of stochastic and coherent noise, making it difficult to extract relevant seismic signals.
skill_point_name: Unified Wavefield Partitioning and Denoising for DAS Data
skill_point_description: Developed a novel framework using curvelets to partition and denoise Distributed Acoustic Sensing data, effectively separating seismic signals from noise. This enabled the identification of over 30% more aftershocks in the Ridgecrest earthquake sequence catalog by removing both stochastic and coherent noise, significantly improving data quality for seismological analysis.

problem_description: Characterizing fault zones at sub-kilometer scales, particularly unmapped or minor ones, is challenging using traditional seismic methods.
skill_point_name: Fault Zone Imaging with Scattered Waves via DAS Backprojection
skill_point_description: Introduced a backprojection technique using DAS-measured scattered earthquake body waves to systematically locate and characterize small-scale fault zones. This method was validated on data from the Ridgecrest earthquake sequence, showing strong spatial correlation between scattering sources and mapped faults, and allowing for the constraint of fault geometry and dimensions, for example, distinguishing between surface-breaching and buried faults.

problem_description: Imaging the depth-dependent structure of narrow fault zones at seismogenic depths is difficult due to limitations in imaging resolution and the integrated nature of traditional measurements.
skill_point_name: Multi-Faceted Depth-Dependent Fault Zone Imaging with DAS
skill_point_description: Implemented a multi-faceted imaging approach using a DAS array across the Garlock Fault to resolve its depth-dependent structure. This involved joint inversion of active source and ambient noise data for shallow structure and utilizing earthquake travel-time observations for deeper insights. The technique revealed a surprisingly narrow low-velocity zone at seismogenic depths, implying significant fault zone healing, and identified a sharp bimaterial contrast suggesting preferred rupture directivity.

problem_description: Traditional methods for mapping Moho topography often lack fine-scale resolution over broad geographic areas due to spatial limitations or noise at low frequencies.
skill_point_name: Fine-Scale Moho Topography Mapping with PmP Phase in DAS Data
skill_point_description: Developed and applied a method to identify and pick relative arrival times of the Moho-reflected PmP phase in high-frequency DAS data, enabling fine-scale mapping of Moho topography. This method leverages the high spatial density and signal coherence of DAS to overcome noise challenges at low frequencies, providing novel observations of sharp Moho changes across key geological features like the Garlock Fault and Coso Volcanic Field.

problem_description: Existing finite-source models often encounter non-uniqueness, require arbitrary parameterization, and limit objective comparisons of earthquake rupture properties.
skill_point_name: Bayesian Inversion of Second Moments for Earthquake Rupture Characterization
skill_point_description: Developed a fully Bayesian inverse scheme to probabilistically determine second moments of the stress glut using teleseismic earthquake seismograms. This low-dimensional representation captures spatiotemporal rupture characteristics extent, duration, directivity without requiring prior knowledge of rupture velocity or detailed fault geometry. Applied to a global catalog of large strike-slip earthquakes, it enabled systematic, error-informed comparisons of rupture properties and revealed patterns related to tectonic environment.

problem_description: Detecting gravitational waves and exploring physics beyond the Standard Model, including dark matter and quantum gravity, using existing and future gravitational wave experiments.
skill_point_name: Multi-Messenger Astronomy for BSM Physics
skill_point_description: This thesis explores novel methodologies to leverage gravitational wave observations from Pulsar Timing Arrays and laser interferometers like LIGO to search for signatures of dark matter and quantum gravity. This involves analyzing pulsar timing measurements for dark matter properties small-scale power spectrum, cosmological phase transitions and interpreting laser interferometer data for macroscopic dark matter signatures and vacuum quantum gravity effects. It highlights the potential of gravitational wave experiments as a new frontier for particle physics.

problem_description: Accurately modeling and detecting dark matter substructures, for example, PBHs and axion miniclusters, that induce subtle shifts in pulsar timing array data, while accounting for astronomical backgrounds and complex signal characteristics.
skill_point_name: Advanced Pulsar Timing Array Data Analysis for Dark Matter Pipeline Development
skill_point_description: Developed and implemented a sophisticated Bayesian inference framework and Monte Carlo simulation pipeline for analyzing realistic PTA data to search for dark matter substructures. This pipeline can model Doppler and Shapiro effects induced by transiting dark matter, differentiate between static and dynamic signals, and compute conditional probability distributions for dark matter abundances. It leverages the NANOGrav 'enterprise' software for robust statistical analysis, demonstrating proficiency in handling astronomical datasets and complex noise characteristics including red noise from SMBHBs.

problem_description: Developing a gauge-invariant framework to calculate the response of laser interferometers to metric perturbations from transiting dark matter, moving beyond simplified accelerator models.
skill_point_name: Gauge-Invariant Interferometer Theory for Dark Matter Detection
skill_point_description: Formally derived the gauge-invariant observable for laser interferometers in the presence of transiting macroscopic dark matter. This involves considering not only the standard Doppler effect mirror acceleration but also the Shapiro delay photon travel time changes and Einstein delay clock proper time dilation. The work provides a comprehensive theoretical basis for interpreting interferometer data for dark matter, including the impact of finite photon travel time, and correctly accounts for tidal and Q-suppression effects in different mass and length scales.

problem_description: Investigating the astrophysical implications of a long-range dark matter-baryon interaction using neutron star observations and pulsar timing arrays.
skill_point_name: Probing Fifth Forces with Astrophysical Observables
skill_point_description: Developed and applied methods to constrain a long-range dark matter-baryon fifth force using two distinct astrophysical phenomena: neutron star kinetic heating and pulsar timing arrays. This involves detailed calculations of energy deposition from transiting dark matter to neutron stars considering both grazing and captured dark matter, and various capture mechanisms including tidal heating and short-range interactions and modeling the Doppler shift in pulsar timing from fifth-force-induced accelerations. The work provides novel constraints on the Yukawa coupling strength across different force ranges.

problem_description: Quantifying and constraining quantum gravity fluctuations in spacetime that manifest as geometric distortions and image blurring in astronomical observations and interferometer measurements.
skill_point_name: Modeling and Constraining Geontropic Spacetime Fluctuations
skill_point_description: Developed and analyzed a 'pixellon' scalar field model to represent quantum gravity fluctuations, geontropic fluctuations, in a causal diamond. This includes deriving the power spectral density and angular correlations of these fluctuations based on principles akin to the Verlinde-Zurek effect. The work applies this model to predict the response of laser interferometers and analyze the blurring effects on astronomical images, demonstrating how holographic principles can lead to observable macroscopic quantum gravity phenomena while remaining consistent with existing observational constraints. It also explores the formal connection between 4D Einstein gravity and 2D Jackiw-Teitelboim JT gravity to study near-horizon quantum dynamics.

problem_description: Rapidly and safely identifying root causes of onboard anomalies in autonomous spacecraft while probabilistically ensuring safety and avoiding collisions.
skill_point_name: Safe Active Fault Estimation s-FEAST
skill_point_description: Develops s-FEAST, an algorithm that extends FEAST to include probabilistic safety constraints for real-time proactive fault estimation. It leverages a marginalized filter for efficient Bayesian updates and concentration inequalities to provide conservative guarantees of safety, allowing diagnostic actions to be taken without inadvertently causing collisions, even in safety-critical scenarios with uncertain dynamics.

problem_description: Inefficient performance of traditional Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithms due to frequent branching and memory access patterns on modern processor architectures, especially GPUs.
skill_point_name: Array-Based MCTS Implementation
skill_point_description: Introduces an array-based implementation of MCTS that redesigns the data structure to make branching operations predictable. This reduces branch misprediction penalties on pipelined processors and leverages existing optimizations for array operations, leading to significantly better scaling with increasing simulation depth in MDP problems and providing a promising direction for hardware acceleration.

problem_description: Autonomous multi-agent systems are vulnerable to stealth attacks that aim to maximize disruption without being detected by the defender.
skill_point_name: Game-Theoretic Stealth Attack Mitigation S3AM
skill_point_description: Formulates the problem of stealth attacks in multi-agent systems as a zero-sum game between an attacker and a defender. Develops the S3AM algorithm, an MCTS-based method that finds optimal reconfigurations for the defender, such as switching observation topologies, to reveal attacks and bound their influence, while also modeling the attacker's optimal strategies to remain undetected.

problem_description: The need for efficient and accurate belief state estimation in partially observable systems, especially when dealing with coupled physical and fault states.
skill_point_name: Marginalized Filtering
skill_point_description: Proposes a marginalized filter that efficiently decomposes the belief over joint physical and fault states into a collection of conditional estimates. This allows for accurate and efficient Bayesian updates, making information-gathering problems tractable for MCTS methods by exploiting the inherent structure of system dynamics and fault models without resorting to full joint state estimation.

problem_description: Optimizing complex, non-convex objectives for spacecraft formation flying missions, both for offline design and real-time reconfiguration.
skill_point_name: Optimal Formation Flying Orbit Planning
skill_point_description: Applies MCTS and genetic algorithms to optimize formation flying orbits for complex mission objectives. This includes offline design for Synthetic Aperture Radar SAR missions balancing science value and cost under operational constraints, and real-time orbit assignment for multi-agent inspection, demonstrating the ability to rapidly reconfigure spacecraft formations for cooperative tasks.

problem_description: Understanding how politicians' communication about media bias impacts democratic accountability and voter selection outcomes.
skill_point_name: Formal Modeling of Strategic Communication
skill_point_description: Developed a novel multi-sender cheap-talk model where an incumbent politician has more information about a media outlet's bias than voters, and evaluates the consequences of politician communication for democratic accountability. This includes analyzing how low-quality politicians use self-serving media criticism as a tactic to skirt accountability, and how voters rationally respond to such messages.

problem_description: Investigating how opposition parties strategically time accusations against political candidates, especially when these accusations trigger investigations that candidates may obstruct.
skill_point_name: Dynamic Game Theory in Political Investigations
skill_point_description: Characterized optimal dynamic obstruction strategies during investigations and modeled an opposition party's decision-making regarding the timing of evidence release. This involves analyzing trade-offs between immediate release for full investigation and late release to minimize belief movement, and how obstruction interacts with voter information and welfare.

problem_description: Analyzing how administrative agencies respond to congressional pressure under different standards of judicial deference, considering its impact on rulemaking speed and quality.
skill_point_name: Modeling Agency Behavior under Political Pressure
skill_point_description: Developed a formal model to understand agency rulemaking processes under varying levels of political insulation and legal deference. This includes insights into how high deference can lead agencies to speed up rulemaking to avoid interference, and how interest groups' preferences for political influence change based on deference standards.

problem_description: Assessing the welfare implications of politician communication and strategic behavior on voter information, selection of representatives, and policy control.
skill_point_name: Welfare Analysis in Political Economy Models
skill_point_description: Conducted detailed welfare analyses comparing equilibrium outcomes across different communication protocols and institutional settings. This involves quantifying improvements or degradations in the electorate's ability to select high-quality representatives, politician behavior, and overall voter welfare under scenarios of hidden actions, complex decision-making, and policy-biased elites.

problem_description: Exploring specific instances where communication or institutional settings can exacerbate problematic behaviors like corruption or anti-media pandering.
skill_point_name: Identifying Mechanisms of Political Malfeasance
skill_point_description: Identified and formally modeled mechanisms through which politician communication can interact with hidden actions, corruption, and observed policymaking, anti-media pandering. This extends the understanding of how discrediting media can be coupled with harmful actions or policy distortions, and how institutional settings can either mitigate or worsen these outcomes.

problem_description: Accurately computing gravitational radiation from Kerr black holes using the Teukolsky equation is numerically challenging due to the long-ranged potential, leading to inaccuracies in numerical solutions.
skill_point_name: Generalized Sasaki-Nakamura GSN Formalism Development
skill_point_description: Developed and revamped the Generalized Sasaki-Nakamura GSN formalism. This involved explicitly showing GSN transformations for physically relevant radiation fields s = 0, ±1, ±2 to convert the radial Teukolsky equation with a long-ranged potential into a new ODE GSN equation with a short-ranged potential. Derived higher-order corrections to asymptotic solutions of the GSN equation and frequency-dependent conversion factors between Teukolsky and GSN formalisms to improve numerical accuracy and efficiency. Implemented an open-source Julia package GeneralizedSasakiNakamura.jl leveraging this revamped formalism.

problem_description: Detecting gravitational-wave echoes from exotic compact objects requires robust data analysis methods to distinguish them from noise and standard black hole merger signals, as well as to estimate their parameters.
skill_point_name: Bayesian Model Selection for GW Echoes Search
skill_point_description: Developed and implemented a template-based Bayesian model selection approach using the log Bayes factor as a detection statistic to search for GW echoes in compact binary coalescence events. This methodology assesses the statistical significance of echo detections against a null hypothesis of no echoes and estimates echo parameters such as amplitude, damping factor, and time delay. The method was rigorously validated with simulated Gaussian noise and real detector noise, and extended to combine evidence from multiple events, allowing for the detection of weak signals in a catalog.

problem_description: Identifying strongly lensed gravitational-wave signals from observations is complex due to various degeneracies, for example, magnification and redshift, and the need to consistently incorporate astrophysical population information and selection effects.
skill_point_name: Hierarchical Bayesian Framework for Gravitational Lensing Identification
skill_point_description: Developed a comprehensive hierarchical Bayesian statistical framework to identify strongly lensed GW signals. This framework models data generation processes for both lensed and not-lensed hypotheses, enabling the computation of a Bayes factor that explicitly incorporates astrophysical population models of GW sources and gravitational lenses, and accounts for selection effects automatically. It includes a scheme to marginalize over the source redshift separately and infer true source parameters using Gibbs sampling, addressing key degeneracies. The framework is implemented in the 'hanabi' Python package.

problem_description: Traditional single-event GW analysis methods are insufficient for optimizing the parameter estimation and sky localization of strongly lensed GW signals, which ideally share common intrinsic parameters and sky locations.
skill_point_name: Joint Parameter Estimation for Lensed GW Signals
skill_point_description: Designed and applied a joint parameter estimation analysis within the Bayesian framework for strongly lensed GW signals. This approach simultaneously analyzes multiple detected GW events or a detected event and sub-threshold counterpart by constructing a joint likelihood function that accounts for shared intrinsic parameters and sky locations, while allowing for different extrinsic parameters, for example, arrival time, apparent luminosity distance. This significantly improves sky localization and provides tighter constraints on source parameters, for example, total mass and redshift, compared to individual analyses, enhancing the ability to locate foreground lenses electromagnetically.

problem_description: Effectively utilizing large catalogs of simulated lensed images for Bayesian inference requires efficient methods for representing and evaluating complex multi-dimensional probability density functions PDFs.
skill_point_name: Normalization Flow for Gravitational Lensing Probability Density Estimation
skill_point_description: Implemented and validated the use of a normalizing-flow-based method denmarf as a surrogate for representing and evaluating complex joint probability density functions PDFs derived from large catalogs of simulated lensed images e.g., magnifications, image types, time delays. This approach offers significant computational advantages over traditional kernel density estimation KDE, as evaluation cost becomes independent of the simulation data size, enabling the practical incorporation of realistic astrophysical lens population models into Bayesian inference for gravitational lensing analysis.

problem_description: Enhancing search sensitivity for weak gravitational wave signals buried in noisy data, particularly when data quality is inconsistent due to non-Gaussian noise glitches.
skill_point_name: Adaptive Ranking Statistic with Data Quality Information
skill_point_description: Developed and proposed a method to incorporate statistical data quality information from the iDQ machine-learning-based pipeline into the GstLAL search pipeline's likelihood ratio calculations. This mitigates the issue of 'polluted' noise background histograms caused by noisy data, preventing unnecessary down-ranking of genuine gravitational wave signals and improving search sensitivity, especially for weaker signals.

problem_description: Ineffective identification of sub-threshold lensed gravitational wave counterparts due to non-optimal template bank construction and lack of a targeted population model, leading to missed signals and high computational costs.
skill_point_name: TESLA-X Method for Targeted Lensed GW Search
skill_point_description: Introduced TESLA-X, an upgraded targeted search method for strongly-lensed sub-threshold gravitational waves. This involves: a novel approach to constructing a reduced template bank that maintains the optimality of the original full template bank within a refined search space, and generating a targeted population model based on kernel density estimation of recovered injection SNRs. This significantly improves search sensitivity and effectiveness in identifying weak lensed signals by better accounting for both signal subspace and noise fluctuations.

problem_description: Prioritizing follow-up of numerous sub-threshold lensed gravitational wave candidates returned by targeted searches, which is computationally expensive and time-consuming without a dedicated ranking metric for lensing consistency.
skill_point_name: Lensing Likelihood for Candidate Ranking
skill_point_description: Developed a 'lensing likelihood' statistic for the TESLA-X pipeline that integrates lens model information. This statistic evaluates how likely a candidate is a lensed counterpart to a target superthreshold event by comparing its relative time delay and magnification with expected distributions from specific lens models. This enables more effective pruning of candidate lists for follow-up, identifying those most consistent with the lensing hypothesis.

problem_description: Analyzing and interpreting the complex characteristics of identified gravitational wave events, for example, GW190412 and GW191103-GW191105, for potential lensing signatures, differentiating them from noise or waveform systematics.
skill_point_name: Multi-Model Lensing Signature Analysis
skill_point_description: Applied and adapted various advanced analysis techniques (Posterior Overlap, Joint Parameter Estimation with HANABI/GOLUM pipelines, Waveform Systematics Study, Microlensing/Millilensing models, EM follow-up cross-matching) to critically assess interesting gravitational wave candidates for strong lensing, microlensing, and millilensing signatures. This involved detailed comparisons with theoretical models and extensive simulation campaigns to understand false alarm probabilities and the robustness of observed features.

problem_description: Quantifying the astrophysical implications of non-detection of lensed gravitational waves, including constraining merger rates and dark matter fractions.
skill_point_name: Astrophysical Constraints from Lensing Search
skill_point_description: Leveraged the non-observation of lensed gravitational waves in O3 data to set constraints on the merger rate density of compact objects at high redshifts and the fraction of dark matter composed of compact objects. This involved calculating expected lensing rates based on various astrophysical population models and using statistical inference to derive upper limits, providing complementary insights to electromagnetic observations.

problem_description: Traditional architected materials suffer from stress concentrations at junctions, limiting their deformability and energy absorption.
skill_point_name: Hierarchical Woven Architectures
skill_point_description: Developed a new 3D hierarchical architecture where fibers are interwoven to construct effective beams, replacing monolithic beams and junctions. This design enables high tensile and compressive strains greater than 50% without failure, smooth reconfiguration, and reduced damage accumulation, offering a pathway to make stiff and brittle materials more deformable.

problem_description: Lack of strategies to enhance energy absorption and shape retention in architected materials.
skill_point_name: Knotted Fiber Topology Integration
skill_point_description: Introduced the concept of knots into the hierarchical architecture framework. This knot topology allows a new deformation regime capable of shape-retention, leading to a significant increase in absorbed energy of approximately 92% and failure strain of approximately 107% compared to woven structures. This unlocks new ways to create shape-reconfigurable, highly extensible, and energy-absorbing materials.

problem_description: Understanding the influence of length scale and surface interactions on the energy dissipation capability of frictional architected materials.
skill_point_name: Adhesion-Friction Size Effect Modeling
skill_point_description: Developed an analytical model based on classical contact mechanics JKR/DMT models and adhesion models to study the effects of structural element length scale on the energy dissipation capability of frictional architected materials. The model predicts that energy dissipation can be significantly increased e.g., >250% higher loss factor when scaled down from mm-scale to sub-micron length scale, highlighting the critical role of work of adhesion.

problem_description: Need for advanced fabrication techniques for micro-architected materials with complex geometries.
skill_point_name: Two-Photon Lithography Fabrication
skill_point_description: Utilized two-photon lithography to precisely fabricate novel micro- and sub-micron scale complex 3D architected materials, including hierarchical woven lattices, intertwined structures with knotted topology, and frictional unit cells. This advanced additive manufacturing technique enabled the realization of intricate fiber geometries and small feature sizes crucial for exploring the proposed designs.

problem_description: Comprehensive mechanical characterization of novel architected materials under various loading conditions and environmental factors.
skill_point_name: Multi-Modal Mechanical Characterization and Analysis
skill_point_description: Performed extensive mechanical testing including in situ quasi-static uniaxial tension, tension-to-compression, and cyclic compression experiments using nanoindenters within SEMs. Investigated the influence of fiber topology, constituent material properties, for example passivation, UV-irradiation, aging, and geometric parameters on mechanical behaviors, providing detailed comparisons with theory and numerical studies.

problem_description: The current knowledge of geopolymeric recycled aggregate concrete GRAC is insufficient to support its safe and reliable application and design.
skill_point_name: Development and Characterization of Sustainable GRAC
skill_point_description: Developed sustainable GRAC using fly ash and ground granulated blast furnace slag as precursors and recycled aggregate as coarse aggregate. Evaluated engineering properties including workability, setting time, density, water absorption, sorptivity, compressive strength, flexural strength, and splitting tensile strength. Microstructural characterization using SEM was also performed.

problem_description: Lack of comprehensive understanding of the static and dynamic compressive behaviors of GRAC, including stress-strain characteristics and energy absorption.
skill_point_name: Static and Dynamic Compressive Behavior Analysis of GRAC
skill_point_description: Investigated quasi-static and dynamic compressive behaviors of GRAC using a high-force servo-hydraulic test system and a Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar apparatus. Analyzed failure patterns, stress-strain curves, and energy absorption capacity. Proposed an empirical model to describe the static stress-strain curve of GRAC and studied the effects of strain rate on dynamic properties.

problem_description: Limited understanding of the failure process and mechanism of GRAC under compression.
skill_point_name: Failure Process and Mechanism Investigation of GRAC using DIC
skill_point_description: Explored the failure process and mechanism of GRAC under static compression with the aid of a digital image correlation system. Monitored and analyzed crack evolution, failure modes, displacement fields, and strain distribution on specimen surfaces to provide detailed insights into the material's behavior.

problem_description: Absence of studies on the behavior of CFRP-confined GRAC under monotonic and cyclic loading, and the applicability of existing models.
skill_point_name: Mechanical Performance Evaluation of CFRP-Confined GRAC
skill_point_description: Conducted experimental studies on the mechanical behaviors of Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Polymer CFRP-confined GRAC under both monotonic and cyclic compression. Investigated failure modes, stress-strain relationships, and axial-lateral strain relationships. Compared results with predictions from existing models to assess their applicability to CFRP-confined GRAC and developed empirical models for ultimate conditions.

problem_description: The need for a summarized review of solid waste recycling in geopolymeric composites and its implications for sustainability.
skill_point_name: Comprehensive Literature Review on Solid Waste Recycling for Geopolymeric Composites
skill_point_description: Conducted an extensive literature review on advanced progress in recycling municipal and construction solid wastes for geopolymeric composites. Summarized the benefits, limitations, characteristic usages, and respective performance of various waste materials in geopolymeric composites, highlighting critical considerations for sustainability and practical implementation.

problem_description: Conventional numerical simulations, for example, FEM, for predicting strain/stress fields are computationally expensive and time-consuming, limiting the exploration of large design spaces for heterogeneous materials.
skill_point_name: AI-based Surrogate Modeling for Continuum-level Physical Fields
skill_point_description: Developed and utilized a conditional generative adversarial network cGAN to directly translate complex material geometries into strain/stress fields in hierarchical composites, bypassing traditional FEM simulations and significantly accelerating property calculation. This method demonstrated capabilities in handling complex nonlinear plasticity, various loading conditions, and hierarchical geometries, even outperforming traditional methods in speed while maintaining high accuracy, exemplified by predicting crack propagation paths consistent with MD simulations.

problem_description: Atomistic simulations, for example MD, for predicting atomic properties in defective crystalline solids are computationally intensive, hindering the exploration of vast structural design spaces.
skill_point_name: GNN-based Atomic Property Prediction in Crystalline Solids
skill_point_description: Implemented Graph Neural Networks GNNs, specifically based on the Principal Neighborhood Aggregation PNA model, to predict atom-wise properties e.g., von Mises stress, potential energy in defective crystalline solids graphene, aluminum. This approach accurately captures local property distributions and physical laws, demonstrating broad applicability across different defect types and material systems, providing a highly efficient alternative to MD simulations.

problem_description: Inverse problems in materials science determining microstructure from observed properties are ill-posed, characterized by limited information and computational challenges, making them intractable for conventional methods.
skill_point_name: Deep Learning for Ill-posed Inverse Problems in Materials
skill_point_description: Proposed a multi-stage deep learning framework combining cGANs and convolutional neural networks to solve inverse problems, specifically to predict complete mechanical fields from partial observations and subsequently identify corresponding material microstructures. This method effectively addresses the 'one-to-many' nature of ill-posed problems by generating multiple plausible solutions and quantifies uncertainty, providing a novel approach for non-destructive characterization and inverse design in both 2D and 3D composites.

problem_description: Material discovery and design often requires high-throughput generation and screening of diverse structures, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive using traditional experimental and computational methods.
skill_point_name: High-throughput Virtual Screening and AI-assisted Property Quantification
skill_point_description: Developed automated high-throughput virtual screening frameworks leveraging atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to generate large datasets of diverse heterogeneous materials, for example, 3D graphene foams, polypeptide self-assemblies. Integrated classical machine learning algorithms, for example, Random Forest, Gaussian Process Regressor, and deep learning models (GNNs) with these datasets for rapid and accurate property quantification, for example, moduli, stress distributions, enabling efficient material design and optimization across structural and compositional heterogeneity.

problem_description: Identifying protein sequences with desired mechanical properties is challenging due to the vast sequence space and the complexity of self-assembly into functional materials.
skill_point_name: Multi-scale Validation and Predictive Modeling for Biomaterials
skill_point_description: Combined high-throughput Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics CGMD simulations with Atomic Force Microscopy AFM experimental validation to accurately determine the mechanical properties of polypeptide self-assemblies. Trained AI-based surrogate models, e.g., Gaussian Process Regressor, on simulation data to efficiently predict the Young's modulus for a significantly larger range of peptide sequences, overcoming the 'peptide sequence challenge' and identifying promising candidates for superior mechanical performance.

problem_description: Systematic tools for characterizing shear-normal coupling properties in arbitrarily complex composite materials remain underdeveloped, and an intuition regarding specific architectural patterns and their direct impact on elastic coupling constants is limited.
skill_point_name: Anisotropic Unit Cell Database Generation and Property Range Estimation
skill_point_description: Developed a method inspired by Cahn's method of generating Gaussian random fields to systematically explore a large property space of anisotropic unit cells. This allowed for the generation of a diverse database of 200,000 unit cells by varying spatial frequencies and thresholds. The property ranges achieved were then compared against theoretical bounds described by hierarchical laminates, identifying regions where hierarchical designs or anisotropic constituents are necessary for extreme elastic anisotropy, especially concerning off-axis parameters.

problem_description: Characterizing the many independent elastic parameters in anisotropic structured materials is complex, especially when shear-normal coupling is present, making it hard to measure even one of the six parameters from a single experiment. No existing experimental methods can measure all stiffness parameters of fully anisotropic structured materials from a single test.
skill_point_name: Single-Test Elastic Parameter Identification using Virtual Fields Method VFM
skill_point_description: Proposed and validated a method based on the Virtual Fields Method to identify all six independent elastic material parameters of plane anisotropic elasticity from a single tension experiment. This method utilizes full-field displacement data obtained via Digital Image Correlation and net reaction forces. Special attention was paid to the choice of virtual fields to minimize errors from boundary effects, ensuring high accuracy comparable to methods requiring multiple tests, especially for structures with at least 10 repeated unit cells. Bayesian linear regression was also applied to quantify uncertainty in parameter identification.

problem_description: Achieving smooth spatial gradients in anisotropic mechanical properties while ensuring the connectivity of adjacent unit cells is challenging, and the mechanical behaviors explored by graded structures designed with anisotropic unit cells are not well studied.
skill_point_name: Design and Analysis of Functionally Graded Anisotropic Metamaterials
skill_point_description: Developed a functional representation method to create functionally graded anisotropic structures with seamless transitions between unit cells. This allowed for independent control of various functional gradients like porosity, anisotropic moduli, and symmetry. Demonstrations included designs eliciting selective elastic energy localization under different loading conditions: tensile, shear, biaxial; and induction of non-affine, rotation-like deformations under simple tensile loading due to geometric incompatibilities in shear-normal coupling moduli.

problem_description: Understanding and engineering wave propagation and mode conversion in complex anisotropic materials dynamically is a new challenge.
skill_point_name: Shear-Longitudinal Wave Mode Conversion in Graded Anisotropic Metamaterials
skill_point_description: Investigated the dispersive behavior of anisotropic unit cells using dynamic numerical homogenization. Demonstrated how functionally graded structures can be engineered to convert shear waves to longitudinal waves and vice versa over a broad range of frequencies. This leverages the hybridization between longitudinal and shear modes in the fundamental modes of anisotropic unit cells.

problem_description: Traditional 3D printing methods, especially for complex geometries, require support structures or post-processing for material removal, and lack precise control over anisotropic properties from complex architectures.
skill_point_name: Advanced Additive Manufacturing for Structured Materials Fabrication
skill_point_description: Utilized advanced multi-material polyjet technology Stratasys Objet500 Connex and Selective Laser Sintering Sintratec Kit 3D printers for fabricating complex anisotropic structured materials and functionally graded designs. Gained expertise in printer assembly, operation, maintenance, and material selection e.g., DM8530 and TangoBlack and optimization of printing parameters to achieve desired mechanical properties and intricate geometries for experimental validation workflows.

problem_description: Traditional composite manufacturing methods are expensive and time-consuming, hindering wider adoption.
skill_point_name: Optimized Out-of-Autoclave Manufacturing
skill_point_description: Developed and perfected economical out-of-autoclave manufacturing methods, Vacuum Bag Only and Hot Pressing for prepregs, and Vacuum Assisted Resin Transfer Molding for dry-fiber infusion, to produce high-quality composite panels with improved cost-effectiveness.

problem_description: Carbon fiber composites suffer from poor through-thickness electrical conductivity and often require separate toughening mechanisms.
skill_point_name: Development of Bi-functional Conductive Interlayers
skill_point_description: Researched and implemented highly conductive carbon veils for existing pre-toughened prepregs and developed novel graphene-coated Polyamide PA veils for resin-infused composites. These PA veils served as bi-functional interlayers, simultaneously enhancing electrical conductivity and interlaminar fracture toughness ILFT.

problem_description: Detecting hard-to-see internal damage in composites without destructive testing is critical for aerospace safety.
skill_point_name: Electrical Resistance Change Method for Structural Health Monitoring
skill_point_description: Applied ERCM to detect through-holes and simulated delaminations in conductive composite panels. Demonstrated higher sensitivity and clearer damage localization in interleaved panels compared to non-interleaved ones, utilizing the enhanced through-thickness electrical conductivity for in-situ damage detection.

problem_description: Understanding the complex interplay between interlayers and mechanical properties, including shear strength, compressive strength, and fracture toughness, is crucial for composite design.
skill_point_name: Comprehensive Mechanical Characterization of Interleaved Composites
skill_point_description: Conducted extensive mechanical testing, including Short Beam Shear, compression, Mode-I ILFT, and Mode-II ILFT tests, to evaluate the impact of interleaved materials on composite mechanical properties. Demonstrated significant improvements in shear strength, compressive strength, and Mode-II ILFT, while analyzing the reduction in Mode-I ILFT for certain interlayer configurations.

problem_description: Ensuring the thermal stability and predictable electrical behavior of conductive composites across varying temperatures is vital for aerospace applications.
skill_point_name: Analysis of Electrical and Dynamic Thermal Behavior of Interleaved Composites
skill_point_description: Investigated the variation of electrical resistance with temperature for interleaved composites, identifying conductor-like behavior in carbon-veil-interleaved CF/epoxy and semiconductor/conductor behavior in graphene-coated PA-interleaved CF/BZ. Performed Dynamic Mechanical Analysis to confirm that the addition of interlayers did not significantly alter the composites' glass transition temperature or dynamic properties.

problem_description: Experimental testing of large, complex discrete multiblock structures for seismic performance is impractical.
skill_point_name: Benchmarking Discrete Element Methods for Seismic Performance
skill_point_description: Developed and benchmarked Level Set Discrete Element Method LS-DEM and Logiciel de Mécanique Gérant le Contact LMGC90 models against experimental shake table data for multiblock concrete structures. This involved calibrating material properties using Monte Carlo sampling and demonstrating the models' ability to predict seismic responses beyond experimental testing limits, offering an efficient framework for simulating stochastic systems.

problem_description: Understanding how design parameters like friction and geometry influence the mechanical properties of architected materials, specifically topologically interlocking materials.
skill_point_name: Computational-Experimental Analysis of Topologically Interlocking Materials
